instruction: Write a Sounio run-pass example named `aggregate_nested_field_deep_copy`. Regression gate for #1479: binding an aggregate local must value-copy its AGGREGATE FIELDS too, not just its outer slots. #1475 fixed the outer copy: `var s2 = s1` stopped aliasing the struct handle,. It should compile and run successfully. Expected stdout: AGGREGATE_NESTED_DEEP_COPY_OK
description: Regression gate for #1479: binding an aggregate local must value-copy its AGGREGATE FIELDS too, not just its outer slots. #1475 fixed the outer copy: `var s2 = s1` stopped aliasing the struct handle,
comments: Regression gate for #1479: binding an aggregate local must value-copy its
AGGREGATE FIELDS too, not just its outer slots.
#1475 fixed the outer copy: `var s2 = s1` stopped aliasing the struct handle,
so a SCALAR field write to the copy was no longer visible through the source.
That copy was FLAT, so a field holding an array or a nested struct still
copied the 64-bit HANDLE — `s2.arr[0] = 99` was observed through `s1`, check
passed, the ELF ran, exit 0, wrong answer. This file pins the deep copy.
GATED TO MADAROS. lean_single INLINES an array-typed struct field
(struct_like_nslots = st_total_size / 8) where Madaros holds it as a handle
(lower_struct_literal_expr_ref, count_struct_fields * 8), so lean_single never
exhibited this bug — but its own `[Struct; N]` and nested-struct handling is a
separate representation with its own boundaries, and pinning both engines from
one file would conflate them. That engine divergence is unchanged by #1479 and
remains open.
KNOWN COST, NOT YET RESOLVED — the deep copy ALLOCATES. A struct with k
aggregate fields needs 1 + k handles per copy instead of 1. The native handle
table is a fixed 1,048,576 entries that is never reclaimed
(native_v2_handle_table_capacity_default, self-hosted/native/gc.sio:36; the
slow path is fail-closed, "no empty-frame reset, live roots not precisely
mapped", exit 182). tests/run-pass/dissertation_pbpk28_parity_ref_rapamycin.sio
copies a 6-array-field struct on every one of its 30,000 CN steps. Measured by
bisecting the step count, the handle ceiling for that program moves from ~110,000
steps to ~26,800 (about 4.1x the handle pressure), leaving it roughly 12% past
the ceiling. Its numbers are UNCHANGED — a reduced-horizon run of the same model
is byte-identical under both compilers, exit 0 both — so the failure is resource
exhaustion, not semantics. That gate is why this change is not landable as it
stands.
STILL DELIBERATELY NOT ASSERTED — an array-of-struct field (`[Inner; N]`).
Copying that array yields fresh element SLOTS whose element handles still
alias; a half-fix in aliasing is how a new miscompile class is born, so those
fields keep the shared handle. Same carve-out #1475 made for `[Struct; N]`
LOCALS.

instruction: Write a Sounio run-pass example named `array_elem_field_store`. Regression test: arr[i].field = value  — store into a field of a struct that is an element of an array-of-structs. Previously NO statement detector matched `name[idx].field = expr` (array. It should compile and run successfully.
description: Regression test: arr[i].field = value  — store into a field of a struct that is an element of an array-of-structs. Previously NO statement detector matched `name[idx].field = expr` (array
comments: Regression test: arr[i].field = value  — store into a field of a struct that
is an element of an array-of-structs.
Previously NO statement detector matched `name[idx].field = expr` (array
index at root, then a field chain): it tokenized as `ident [ .. ] . ident =`
and fell through to expression-statement handling, silently dropping the
store or segfaulting. The `name.field[i] = v` (leaf-index) path was a
different, already-handled case.
Fix in lean_single.sio: stmt_is_array_elem_field_store +
compile_array_elem_field_store_x86. Array-of-struct slots hold pointers to
heap-materialized copies, so each slot must first be populated with a whole
struct (arr[i] = S{..}) before per-field mutation.
Covers: local array root, &![T;N] ref-param root, and a nested field chain
(arr[i].inner.v). Global arrays-of-structs are a separate, pre-existing
limitation (the global subscript read path supports only esz==8/esz==1, not
inline structs), so they are out of scope here.

instruction: Write a Sounio run-pass example named `array_init_survives_O`. #1682: `-O` deleted the register holding an array initialiser's fill value. IrIndexSet has THREE register operands -- base, index, value -- but IrInstr has only src1/src2, so ir_index_set parks the value in `imm_i64`. An immediate. It should compile and run successfully. Expected stdout: a0=7 a3=7 b0=7 b1=5 sum=5
description: #1682: `-O` deleted the register holding an array initialiser's fill value. IrIndexSet has THREE register operands -- base, index, value -- but IrInstr has only src1/src2, so ir_index_set parks the value in `imm_i64`. An immediate
comments: #1682: `-O` deleted the register holding an array initialiser's fill value.
IrIndexSet has THREE register operands -- base, index, value -- but IrInstr
has only src1/src2, so ir_index_set parks the value in `imm_i64`. An immediate
slot holding a register is exactly what a liveness scan does not look at, and
ocp_mfi_dce_once scanned src1/src2 only. `[7; 4]` lowers to a fill loop whose
sole use of the 7 is that field, so the defining load_imm was removed as dead
and the array was filled with garbage.
Before the fix, under -O: a0=0 a3=0 b0=0 b1=0 sum=0. On origin/main the same
program HANGS under -O.
This test is only meaningful when run WITH -O; without it the pass does not
run and it passes vacuously. It deliberately covers all three shapes: read
after init only, read after a partial store, and a fill loop feeding a helper
through a reference.

description: Regression test: bare &![T; N] array parameter mutation visible to caller. Previously broken (JIT/codegen): when passing a bare array variable by &! exclusive reference, mutations inside the callee via `arr[i] = v` (without
comments: Regression test: bare &![T; N] array parameter mutation visible to caller.
Previously broken (JIT/codegen): when passing a bare array variable by &!
exclusive reference, mutations inside the callee via `arr[i] = v` (without
explicit deref) were not visible to the caller because the codegen path for
arr[i] = v on a &![T;N] parameter was not distinguishing array-refs from
plain scalars and emitting a byte store instead of a qword store.
Fix in lean_single.sio: stmt_is_array_store and the primary array-read path
now check VAR_TY == 10 with inner type == 8 and set is_arr_ty = 1, causing
the correct `mov [rax + rcx*8], rdx` 8-byte store to be emitted.
This test confirms all three mutation patterns work:
1. Bare index: arr[i] = v  (was broken)
2. Explicit deref: (*arr)[i] = v  (always worked)
3. Struct wrapper: b.field[i] = v  (always worked)

instruction: Write a Sounio run-pass example named `bignat_selftest`. Self-contained selftest for the arbitrary-precision SIGNED BigInt built on top of the unsigned base-1e9-limb BigNat core (see stdlib/math/bignat.sio for the canonical, documented, reusable version of this same code). It should compile and run successfully.
description: Self-contained selftest for the arbitrary-precision SIGNED BigInt built on top of the unsigned base-1e9-limb BigNat core (see stdlib/math/bignat.sio for the canonical, documented, reusable version of this same code).
comments: Self-contained selftest for the arbitrary-precision SIGNED BigInt built on
top of the unsigned base-1e9-limb BigNat core (see stdlib/math/bignat.sio
for the canonical, documented, reusable version of this same code).
Self-contained (no `use`/import) per the #637 large-by-value-struct
cross-module SIGSEGV flake: BigNat embeds a [i64; 64] limb array, and
signed ops thread BigNat/BigInt (and UnatDivRes/BigDivRes wrapping two of
them) through struct-return call chains -- keeping everything in one
module avoids that boundary entirely.
IMPORTANT CALIBRATION NOTE (found empirically this session, souc v0.80.0):
this compiler build has a separate, real whole-program codegen capacity
wall that is NOT the documented module-boundary flake. Once a single
compiled program combines "too many" struct-heavy (BigNat/BigInt-by-value)
functions and call-sites in one `main`, madaros can SIGSEGV during codegen
-- or, more dangerously, silently emit WRONG VALUES (observed: swapped
add/sub results, sign flips, corrupted digits) with a clean exit and no
diagnostic. The threshold is not a simple statement or function count; it
is sensitive to exact code shape/order and was NOT fixed by shrinking the
struct (LIMBS 64->4 made no difference), which rules out a byte-size
budget and points to a stack/spill-slot table sized for a fixed number of
large-aggregate call sites. Every individual op below (add/sub/mul/cmp/
divmod/gcd) was verified byte-for-byte correct against Python arbitrary
precision (scripts/research/bignat_oracle.py) in *isolation* first -- this
file exercises the exact, empirically-proven-safe combination (6 ops, one
divmod call, one gcd call) that stays under that wall. Additional ops
(signed add/sub/mul with negative operands, eq, is_zero) that could not
safely coexist with these in the SAME compiled program are covered in the
companion files bignat_selftest_signed.sio, bignat_selftest_eq_true.sio,
bignat_selftest_eq_false.sio, bignat_selftest_iszero_true.sio,
bignat_selftest_iszero_false.sio -- each independently verified correct.
Do not merge these files back into one without re-verifying every printed
value against the Python oracle: this wall silently corrupts arithmetic,
it does not always crash.
Values exceed i64 (max ~9.2e18): 10^30, 10^20, their sum/difference,
bit-for-bit against scripts/research/bignat_oracle.py.
big_divmod / big_gcd use TRUNCATING division (toward zero); the case
exercised here uses non-negative operands, so this matches Python's
`//`/`%` exactly (Python's floor-toward -inf convention would otherwise
diverge from truncation on negative operands -- see stdlib/math/bignat.sio
module doc comment).

comments: causal_graph_dsep.sio
A causal graph declared in source, and independence claims discharged against
it by d-separation. Before this the claim was only checked for degeneracy: it
could be written, never proven, and the composition law in

comments: The e_top-seam bridge is a Cayley-Dickson TOWER phenomenon, certified at dim 16, 32, 64.
In the sedenion brick (sedenion_seam_bridge.sio) the operator non-anticommutation, the state-level
zero-division, and the e₈ seam were shown to be one locus. This brick certifies that the SAME
coincidence holds at the next levels of the Cayley-Dickson tower: for the 2ⁿ-dim algebra A_n with top
imaginary unit e_top (top = 2ⁿ⁻¹), and lower×upper index-pairs (l ∈ 1..top-1, u ∈ top..2ⁿ-1):
{L_l, L_u} ≠ 0   ⟺   (L_l L_u)² ≠ −I   ⟺   e_l + e_u is a left zero divisor   ⟺   off the e_top seam.
PROVED (dimension-independent, not per-level): once L_l² = L_u² = −I, the forward obstruction is pure
linear algebra — {L_l,L_u}=0 ⟹ (L_lL_u)² = −L_l²L_u² = −I ⟹ +1 ∉ spec ⟹ L_l+L_u nonsingular ⟹
e_l+e_u is not a ZD; and (L_l+L_u singular ⟺ +1∈spec ⟺ e_l+e_u a ZD) is linear algebra too. The
spectral/singular members therefore need no computation. The base fact L_i²=−I is the cocycle lemma
σ(i,j)·σ(i,i⊕j) = −1   (all i≥1, all j),
certified here at each dim (and proved by induction on bits in the Lean leg → forward holds for ALL n).
COMPUTED here (the content — that two independently-defined sets coincide): the non-anticommuting set,
the zero-divisor set, and the off-seam set are equal. Sizes = (top-1)(top-2) [= number of off-seam
pairs by definition; a footnote, not the result]: 42, 210, 930 at dim 16, 32, 64.
OPEN (all n): the CONVERSE off-seam ⟹ ZD is verified at n=4,5,6, not proved — a tower-wide conjecture.
Sizes: dim 64 zero-divisor scan is left to the oracle (kept out of this test to stay fast); here dim 64
certifies the cocycle lemma + the operator/seam coincidence + counts. Decidable integer arithmetic.
SELF-CONTAINED. Cross-verified vs the oracle + Lean.

use epistemic::proof_carrying_path_conditioned_identification::*

fn main() with Panic {
    let d8_ab = ExactABIdentifiedSetReceipt {
        set_id: 12301,
        model_id: 12200,
        model_version: 1,
        assumption_set_id: 12210,

        path_code: 1,

        scalar_projection: 877,

        sound_outer: true,
        witnessed_inner: true,
        heuristic: false,

        confidence_region: false,
        predictive_set: false,
    }
    let target = bind_d8_exact_set_as_d9_coverage_target(20001, d8_ab)
    assert(target.member_mask == 3 && target.member_count == 2)
    assert(target.exact_within_frozen_d8_family)
    assert(!target.confidence_region && !target.predictive_set)
    assert(!target.patient_state)

    assert(procedure.outcome_count == 4)
    assert(procedure.outcome_0_region_mask == 3)
    assert(procedure.outcome_1_region_mask == 1)
    assert(procedure.outcome_2_region_mask == 2)
    assert(procedure.outcome_3_region_mask == 7)
    assert(procedure.whole_set_coverage_target)
    assert(!procedure.memberwise_coverage_target)

    let design_a = declare_d9_sampling_design_a(20101, procedure)
    let design_b = declare_d9_sampling_design_b(20102, procedure)
    assert(design_a.weight_0 == 5 && design_a.weight_1 == 1)
    assert(design_a.weight_2 == 1 && design_a.weight_3 == 5)
    assert(design_b.weight_0 == 1 && design_b.weight_1 == 5)
    assert(design_b.weight_2 == 5 && design_b.weight_3 == 1)
    assert(design_a.total_mass == 12 && design_b.total_mass == 12)
    assert(design_a.sampling_positivity_in_fixture)
    assert(design_b.sampling_positivity_in_fixture)
    assert(!design_a.real_sampling_law && !design_b.real_sampling_law)

    let whole_a = enumerate_d9_whole_set_coverage_a(
        20201, target, procedure, design_a,
    )
    let whole_b = enumerate_d9_whole_set_coverage_b(
        20202, target, procedure, design_b,
    )
    let member_a = enumerate_d9_memberwise_coverage_a(20211, design_a)
    let member_b = enumerate_d9_memberwise_coverage_b(20212, design_b)
    assert(whole_a.numerator == 10 && whole_a.denominator == 12)
    assert(whole_a.permille_floor == 833 && whole_a.permille_remainder == 4)
    assert(whole_b.numerator == 2 && whole_b.denominator == 12)
    assert(whole_b.permille_floor == 166 && whole_b.permille_remainder == 8)
    assert(member_a.minimum_member_coverage_numerator == 11)
    assert(member_b.minimum_member_coverage_numerator == 7)
    assert(whole_a.simultaneous_whole_set_coverage)
    assert(whole_b.simultaneous_whole_set_coverage)
    assert(member_a.memberwise_coverage && member_b.memberwise_coverage)

    let adequate = certify_d9_adequate_coverage(20301, whole_a)
    let insufficient = refuse_d9_insufficient_coverage(20302, whole_b)
    assert(adequate.left_cross_product == 40)
    assert(adequate.right_cross_product == 36 && adequate.adequate)
    assert(insufficient.left_cross_product == 8)
    assert(insufficient.right_cross_product == 36)
    assert(!insufficient.adequate_coverage_issued)

        20402, procedure, design_b, whole_b,

    assert(region_a.member_mask == 3 && region_b.member_mask == 3)
    assert(region_a.lower_state_code == region_b.lower_state_code)
    assert(region_a.upper_state_code == region_b.upper_state_code)
    assert(region_a.design_id != region_b.design_id)
    assert(region_a.coverage_id != region_b.coverage_id)
    assert(region_a.coverage_attaches_to_procedure)
    assert(!region_a.per_realization_truth_probability)
    assert(!region_a.exact_identified_set && !region_a.predictive_set)

    let predictive = declare_d9_predictive_set(20403)
    assert(predictive.response_mask == 3)
    assert(predictive.future_response_target)
    assert(!predictive.identified_set_target)
    assert(!predictive.confidence_region_target)
    assert(!predictive.individual_conditional_coverage)

    let marginal = record_d9_marginal_coverage(20501)
    let rare = record_d9_rare_group_failure(20502)
    let selected = record_d9_selection_coverage_failure(20503, rare)
    let selection_abstention = abstain_on_d9_selection_failure(20504, selected)
    assert(marginal.covered_count == 9 && marginal.total_count == 10)
    assert(rare.covered_count == 0 && rare.total_count == 1)
    assert(selected.selected_subgroup_id == 20511)
    assert(!selected.valid_selected_coverage)
    assert(selection_abstention.reason_mask == 2)
    assert(!selection_abstention.negative_prediction_issued)
    assert(!selection_abstention.clinical_escalation_issued)
    assert(!selection_abstention.clinical_action_issued)

    let lineage_a = declare_d9_provenance_a(20601, region_a)
    let lineage_b = declare_d9_provenance_b(20602, region_b)
    let mismatch = refuse_d9_provenance_substitution(
        20603, lineage_a, lineage_b,
    )
    assert(lineage_a.table_fingerprint == lineage_b.table_fingerprint)
    assert(lineage_a.realized_region_mask == lineage_b.realized_region_mask)
    assert(!lineage_a.integrity_verified && !lineage_a.authenticity_verified)
    assert(!lineage_a.external_custody_sealed)
    assert(mismatch.distinct_dataset_ids)
    assert(mismatch.distinct_instrument_versions)
    assert(mismatch.distinct_population_versions)
    assert(mismatch.distinct_windows)
    assert(!mismatch.lineages_substitutable)

    let population = declare_d9_target_population(20701)
    let window = declare_d9_target_time_window(20702)
    let positivity = certify_d9_sampling_positivity(20801, design_a, population)
    let positivity_failure = record_d9_sampling_positivity_failure(20802)
    let coverage_calibration = certify_d9_finite_coverage_calibration(

    assert(positivity.sampling_support_positive)

    assert(!positivity_failure.sampling_support_positive)
    assert(coverage_calibration.finite_fixture_calibrated)
    assert(!coverage_calibration.metrological_calibration)
    assert(!coverage_calibration.external_calibration)
    assert(!coverage_failure.finite_fixture_calibrated)
    assert(instrument_calibration.metrological_calibration_current)
    assert(!instrument_calibration.statistical_coverage_calibration)
    assert(!instrument_failure.metrological_calibration_current)
    assert(compatibility.compatible && !incompatibility.compatible)
    assert(matched.explicit_identity_match && !matched.external_custody_sealed)

    let declared = bind_d9_declared_fixture_context(
        20901, region_a, adequate, population, window, positivity,

        21002, external,

    assert(external_abstention.reason_mask == 230)
    assert(external_abstention.model_criticism_recorded)
    assert(!external_abstention.empirical_binding_issued)
    assert(!external_abstention.patient_state_issued)
    assert(!external_abstention.clinical_authority_issued)

    assert(!causal_ambiguity.action_direction_identified)
    assert(!causal_ambiguity.clinical_authority_issued)

    let summary = summarize_d9_statistical_coverage(
        21201, declared, external_abstention,

    assert(summary.synthetic_design_count == 455)
    assert(summary.positive_design_count == 165)

description: Smoke test: cross-compilation target flag parsing and codegen dispatch. The Mach-O (write_macho_x86 / write_macho_arm64) and PE/COFF (write_pe) backends were implemented but previously undocumented as "not yet wired".  They are in fact
comments: Smoke test: cross-compilation target flag parsing and codegen dispatch.
The Mach-O (write_macho_x86 / write_macho_arm64) and PE/COFF (write_pe) backends
were implemented but previously undocumented as "not yet wired".  They are in fact
dispatched by the codegen driver in main() based on TARGET_OS / TARGET_ARCH:
--target x86_64-linux   → TARGET_OS=0, TARGET_ARCH=0 → write_elf()       (default)
--target aarch64-linux  → TARGET_OS=0, TARGET_ARCH=1 → write_elf_arm64()
--target x86_64-macos   → TARGET_OS=2, TARGET_ARCH=0 → write_macho_x86()
--target aarch64-macos  → TARGET_OS=2, TARGET_ARCH=1 → write_macho_arm64()
--target x86_64-windows → TARGET_OS=3, TARGET_ARCH=0 → write_pe()
This file is a minimal Sounio program that compiles and runs correctly on Linux
(the host platform).  The cross-compilation targets require running the produced
binary on the corresponding OS; the compiler itself will emit a valid Mach-O or
PE/COFF file when invoked with the appropriate --target flag.
To manually verify cross-compile flag acceptance:
$SOUC compile tests/run-pass/cross_compile_flag.sio -o /tmp/out.macho --target x86_64-macos
$SOUC compile tests/run-pass/cross_compile_flag.sio -o /tmp/out.pe    --target x86_64-windows
Both commands should succeed with exit code 0 and emit the respective binary format.

instruction: Write a Sounio run-pass example named `dissertation_pbpk14_hessian`. tests/run-pass/dissertation_pbpk14_hessian.sio End-to-end demonstration of the second-order GUM Hessian propagator. Two halves:. It should compile and run successfully.
description: tests/run-pass/dissertation_pbpk14_hessian.sio End-to-end demonstration of the second-order GUM Hessian propagator. Two halves:
comments: tests/run-pass/dissertation_pbpk14_hessian.sio
End-to-end demonstration of the second-order GUM Hessian propagator.
Two halves:
(1) Synthetic-output residual proof.  For a controlled non-linear
endpoint y = a · x², the analytic variance is closed-form.  We
compute it three ways: ground truth, GUM 1st order (Jacobian),
GUM 2nd order (Jacobian + Hessian correction).  The acceptance
check is |GUM_2nd − truth| < |GUM_1st − truth| — the dissertation
claim that the 2nd-order term moves the GUM estimate toward the
true variance for non-linear outputs.
(2) Rapamycin AUC Hessian budget.  Runs the propagator on a
2-parameter rapamycin sub-case (CL_hep × fu_plasma) and emits a
CSV-format budget.  The companion gate redirects this section
to benchmarks/pbpk/hessian_budget.csv.
Final stdout line: "PASS hessian_correction_reduces_residual"

instruction: Write a Sounio run-pass example named `dissertation_pbpk14_model_form_uc`. DISSERTATION: PBPK-14 MODEL-FORM UNCERTAINTY → GUM RISK BUDGET (roi.sio) Reads the committed benchmark CSV benchmarks/pbpk/model_form_uc.csv at runtime (read_file, no embedded data) and aggregates the model-form. It should compile and run successfully. Expected stdout: ALL TESTS PASSED — ONE model-form risk term; the two aggregations
description: DISSERTATION: PBPK-14 MODEL-FORM UNCERTAINTY → GUM RISK BUDGET (roi.sio) Reads the committed benchmark CSV benchmarks/pbpk/model_form_uc.csv at runtime (read_file, no embedded data) and aggregates the model-form
comments: DISSERTATION: PBPK-14 MODEL-FORM UNCERTAINTY → GUM RISK BUDGET (roi.sio)
Reads the committed benchmark CSV benchmarks/pbpk/model_form_uc.csv at
runtime (read_file, no embedded data) and aggregates the model-form
discrepancy between the 28-compartment literature reference model
(c_pbpk28_lit) and the 14-compartment well-stirred reduced model
(c_pbpk14_wellstirred) BOTH ways, to show the GUM model-form term is
robust to the aggregation choice:
METHOD 1 — AUC-weighted residual fraction
Per organ:  resid1_o = |AUC28_o - AUC14_o| / AUC28_o
where AUC_o = trapezoidal integral of C_o(t) over the sample times.
Aggregate scalar (exposure-weighted across organs):
resid1 = Σ_o |AUC28_o - AUC14_o| / Σ_o AUC28_o
The 28-compartment model is the truth reference (denominator).
METHOD 2 — Peak-window residual fraction (t ≤ 6 h)
Restrict to the early/peak window where absolute exposure is highest.
Exposure-weighted (concentration-mass-weighted) relative delta:
resid2 = Σ_{t≤6h,o} |C28 - C14| / Σ_{t≤6h,o} C28
NEAR-ZERO-TAIL GUARD: the CSV's delta_pct hits 1246% at the brain
t=30h sample where C28 ≈ 1e-6. Because BOTH methods weight by absolute
exposure (AUC magnitude / concentration mass), that late-time tail is
negligible in the numerator AND denominator and CANNOT dominate. We do
NOT use the raw delta_pct column for the residual fraction.
CSV columns (verified header):
t_hours, organ_idx, organ_name, c_pbpk28_lit, c_pbpk14_wellstirred,
delta_abs, delta_pct
(delta_pct is normalized by c_pbpk14, NOT the reference — so it is NOT
used as the residual fraction; we recompute from the two C columns.)
EPISTEMIC RISK LEDGER WIRING (stdlib/epistemic/roi.sio):
risk_model_form(source, residual_fraction) → ModelRisk
risk_bits = log2(1 + residual_fraction)   [information-theoretic risk/
debt accounting, Contrib. 2 — NOT a GUM standard-uncertainty/variance]
ledger_add_risk(ledger, risk) accumulates risk_total_bits.
The two aggregation methods are alternative ESTIMATES of the SAME model-
form discrepancy, so they are NOT summed (that double-counts one source);
the ledger holds ONE term (conservative peak-window) and the two methods
bracket its magnitude as a sensitivity range.
Reference model: 28-compartment literature PBPK (truth)
Reduced model:   14-compartment perfusion-limited well-stirred PBPK

expect-stdout: ALL TESTS PASSED — ONE model-form risk term; the two aggregations

instruction: Write a Sounio run-pass example named `dissertation_pbpk28_confidence_gate`. PBPK28 rapamycin priors carried as Knowledge<f64> with literature ε. It should compile and run successfully.
description: PBPK28 rapamycin priors carried as Knowledge<f64> with literature ε.
comments: These are the real rapamycin priors from stdlib/darwin_pbpk/epistemic_pbpk28.sio
(ep28_rapamycin_priors), where confidence was a plain f64 the type system could
not see. Carried as Knowledge<f64, ε> they become first-class: the ε flows into
the EpistemicComplete gate, so a function cannot claim more confidence than its
weakest input supports.
cl_hepatic ε=0.65 (Jiao/Zhang 2009 pop-PK, CV≈38%)
fu_plasma  ε=0.72 (Schreiber 1991, CV≈25%)
kp_liver   ε=0.60 (Valoteau 1996, CV≈25%)
kp_adipose ε=0.40 (capped model, CV≈40%)   ← the weakest evidence
Gate semantics (per-token, NOT combined): `with Epistemic(N)` requires EVERY
input expression to individually carry confidence ≥ N. It does NOT certify the
propagated/combined confidence of the result (that compounds far lower). So the
maximum satisfiable N is the WEAKEST single prior, kp_adipose ε=0.40 → 400:
verified that Epistemic(400) compiles but Epistemic(401) already rejects (and
Epistemic(650) flags both kp_adipose and kp_liver). This is the type system
refusing to let any under-evidenced input enter a high-confidence claim.

instruction: Write a Sounio run-pass example named `dissertation_pbpk28_degenerate_parity_ref`. DISSERTATION PBPK28 PARITY REFERENCE — DEGENERATE (V_v→0, PS→∞) Companion to website/src/lib/pbpk28_core.mjs and the parity gate at scripts/ci/dissertation_pbpk28_parity_gate.sh (Case 2: asymptotic reduction. It should compile and run successfully.
description: DISSERTATION PBPK28 PARITY REFERENCE — DEGENERATE (V_v→0, PS→∞) Companion to website/src/lib/pbpk28_core.mjs and the parity gate at scripts/ci/dissertation_pbpk28_parity_gate.sh (Case 2: asymptotic reduction
comments: DISSERTATION PBPK28 PARITY REFERENCE — DEGENERATE (V_v→0, PS→∞)
Companion to website/src/lib/pbpk28_core.mjs and the parity gate at
scripts/ci/dissertation_pbpk28_parity_gate.sh (Case 2: asymptotic reduction
of PBPK28 → PBPK14 well-stirred).
Degenerate configuration:
vasc_frac_at(i) = 1e-3 ∀ organs (vs 0.019–0.282 in the literature ref)
ps_at(i)        = lit_PS_i × 1e4   (drives PS-coupling instantaneous)
At these parameters CN's A-stability is essential — explicit RK4 in the
slow operator would require dt ~ 1e-7 h for kidney/lung; CN integrates
stably at dt = 0.001 h.
CORRECTED asymptotic claim (G-α-β math correction):
PBPK28 at (V_v → 0, PS → ∞) does NOT reduce to PBPK14 well-stirred. It
reduces to a *1-state quasi-steady-state (QSS) model*:
V_eff · dC_b/dt = -cl_hep · C_b + release,
V_eff = V_b + Σ V_i · Kp_i
C_v_i = C_b instantly; C_t_i = Kp_i · C_b instantly.
PBPK14 well-stirred sits BETWEEN PBPK28-lit (finite PS, finite V_v) and
PBPK28-degenerate (V_v→0, PS→∞). The three models form a hierarchy in
model-form complexity; PBPK14 is the *intermediate* approximation where
tissue redistributes instantly *within* an organ but blood-to-tissue
transport remains rate-limited by Q. PBPK28-degenerate additionally
assumes blood-to-tissue transport is also instantaneous.
This file remains useful as: (a) the target trajectory for the
fully-coupled CN A-stability proof at extreme stiffness, and (b) the
numerical demonstration that PBPK28-degenerate matches the 1-state QSS
limit (asymptotic verification of the model-reduction theorem).
Quantitative match against the 1-state QSS limit at literature
parameters provides the Type B model-form uncertainty contribution per
JCGM 100:2008 §4.3 (the G-α-γ follow-up will emit benchmarks/pbpk/
model_form_uc.csv from these comparisons).
Model: permeability-limited PBPK, 14 organs × {vascular, interstitial}.
V_v,i · dC_v,i/dt = Q_i·(C_blood - C_v,i) - PS_i·(C_v,i - C_t,i/Kp_i)
V_t,i · dC_t,i/dt = PS_i·(C_v,i - C_t,i/Kp_i)
V_b   · dC_b/dt   = sum_i Q_i·(C_v,i - C_b) - cl_hep·C_b
Integrator: fully-coupled Crank-Nicolson on the 27-state PBPK28 system —
no operator splitting. PS coupling and Q transport integrated implicitly in
one CN step via per-organ Schur-complement elimination + scalar reduction
for C_blood. A-stable, 2nd-order, no splitting-induced bias.
Compartment indexing matches website/src/components/dissertation/compartments.ts:
0=blood 1=liver 2=kidney 3=brain 4=heart 5=lung 6=muscle 7=adipose
8=gut   9=skin  10=bone   11=spleen 12=pancreas 13=other
Bolus 0.05 mg into blood (C_blood(0) = 0.01 mg/L). cl_hep = 12.4 L/h. Stent off.
Twelve log-spaced sample times. Emits PARITY|t / PARITY|i / PARITY|cv / PARITY|ct
/ PARITY|cavg records — the gate joins on (t, i) and compares against the
Node runner's identical output.

instruction: Write a Sounio run-pass example named `dissertation_pbpk28_parity_ref_midazolam`. DISSERTATION PARITY REFERENCE — MIDAZOLAM (CYP3A drug–drug interaction) Fifth canonical drug, and the suite's FIRST drug–drug interaction (DDI). Novel surface (none of rapamycin/semaglutide/venlafaxine/haloperidol model enzyme. It should compile and run successfully.
description: DISSERTATION PARITY REFERENCE — MIDAZOLAM (CYP3A drug–drug interaction) Fifth canonical drug, and the suite's FIRST drug–drug interaction (DDI). Novel surface (none of rapamycin/semaglutide/venlafaxine/haloperidol model enzyme
comments: DISSERTATION PARITY REFERENCE — MIDAZOLAM (CYP3A drug–drug interaction)
Fifth canonical drug, and the suite's FIRST drug–drug interaction (DDI). Novel
surface (none of rapamycin/semaglutide/venlafaxine/haloperidol model enzyme
inhibition): mechanistic well-stirred oral first-pass + competitive CYP3A
inhibition by ketoconazole.
Oral bioavailability   F     = Fa · FG · FH
gut-wall survival      FG    = Qg / (Qg + fu_g·CLint_g)
hepatic first-pass     FH    = Qh / (Qh + fu·CLint_h)
systemic clearance     CL_h  = Qh·fu·CLint_h / (Qh + fu·CLint_h)
competitive inhibition CLint -> CLint / (1 + I/Ki)   (gut & hepatic, same enzyme)
A SINGLE hepatic intrinsic clearance CLint_h drives BOTH FH and CL_h, so
inhibition raises FH and lowers CL_h consistently — NO double-count — and the
iconic oral midazolam+ketoconazole AUC rise (~15×) emerges honestly
(AUC = F·Dose/CL_h). The inhibitor is held STATIC at its steady-state unbound
concentration (as in clinical DDI studies). Systemic distribution Kp are
nominal midazolam-plausible values; the validated DDI quantities are F, CL_h
and AUCR (distribution-independent).
Both this ref and the JS engine (pbpk28_core.mjs runMidazolamScenario /
runMidazolamDDIResponse) use a FIXED-STEP RK4 systemic integrator at the same
dt — the production scenario (scenarios/oral_midazolam_ddi.sio) uses adaptive
Tsit5, an intractable bit-for-bit parity target; the fidelity gap is disclosed
in the gist. Self-contained (no imports — lean_single blocks cross-module
private fields); all constants verbatim from drugs/midazolam.sio +
ddi/cyp3a_competitive.sio.
Parity surface (gate cases 17-19): solo oral PK · ketoconazole-inhibited oral
PK · DDI inhibition curve (F, CL_h, AUCR across I/Ki).
Sources: Heizmann 1984 (oral F~0.4), Thummel 1996 (gut+hepatic first-pass),
Gorski 1998 / Olkkola 1994,1996 (ketoconazole DDI ~15×), Yang 2007 (Qgut).

instruction: Write a Sounio run-pass example named `dissertation_pbpk_qss_analytical_ref`. DISSERTATION 1-STATE QSS ANALYTICAL REFERENCE — RAPAMYCIN Closed-form quasi-steady-state limit of PBPK28 at (V_v → 0, PS → ∞): V_eff · dC_b/dt = -cl_hep · C_b + release. It should compile and run successfully.
description: DISSERTATION 1-STATE QSS ANALYTICAL REFERENCE — RAPAMYCIN Closed-form quasi-steady-state limit of PBPK28 at (V_v → 0, PS → ∞): V_eff · dC_b/dt = -cl_hep · C_b + release
comments: DISSERTATION 1-STATE QSS ANALYTICAL REFERENCE — RAPAMYCIN
Closed-form quasi-steady-state limit of PBPK28 at (V_v → 0, PS → ∞):
V_eff · dC_b/dt = -cl_hep · C_b + release
V_eff = V_b + Σ V_i · Kp_i
C_b(0+) = M_0 / V_eff (instantaneous redistribution)
C_b(t) = C_b(0+) · exp(-cl_hep · t / V_eff)
C_avg_i(t) = Kp_i · C_b(t)   [i ≥ 1];  C_avg_0(t) = C_b(t)
Consumed by scripts/ci/dissertation_pbpk28_parity_gate.sh Case 2 — the gate
compares the PBPK28 fully-coupled-CN degenerate trajectory against this
analytical limit and reports the convergence residual as the Type B
model-form uncertainty contribution per JCGM 100:2008 §4.3.
CORRECTED MATH (commits c574ee81 + this commit):
PBPK28 at (V_v→0, PS→∞) does NOT reduce to PBPK14. It reduces to *this*
1-state QSS model. PBPK14 well-stirred is the *intermediate* model where
within-organ redistribution is instantaneous but Q-transport between
blood and tissue remains rate-limited. The hierarchy is
PBPK28-literature → PBPK14 → 1-state QSS
with monotonically decreasing model-form complexity. Discrepancies
between successive tiers are Type B uncertainty contributions.
Parameters and 12 sample times match
tests/run-pass/dissertation_pbpk28_parity_ref_rapamycin.sio.

instruction: Write a Sounio run-pass example named `epistemic_var_accumulator_slots`. Regression pin for #1535: a mutable local must carry its uncertainty across reassignment, including when it was initialised from an EXPRESSION and when the reassignment happens inside a loop. It should compile and run successfully. Expected stdout: VAR_ACCUM_OK
description: Regression pin for #1535: a mutable local must carry its uncertainty across reassignment, including when it was initialised from an EXPRESSION and when the reassignment happens inside a loop.
comments: Regression pin for #1535: a mutable local must carry its uncertainty across
reassignment, including when it was initialised from an EXPRESSION and when the
reassignment happens inside a loop.
Two defects sat here, and the second hid behind the first:
1. Assignment REBOUND the local's variance/sens to the RHS's fresh vregs
instead of copying into fixed slots. A rebind is a compile-time map update
and a loop body's IR is emitted once, so every iteration recomputed from
the pre-loop uncertainty and only one iteration's contribution survived.
2. The fix for (1) allocated those slots BEFORE the branches that bind a
declaration's variance from its RHS, so those branches overwrote them.
Only a literal-initialised local escaped, because a literal leaves those
branches nothing to bind.
Truth values below are first-order GUM propagation, computed independently
rather than read off either engine. var(cl) = 1.24^2 = 1.5376.
TEST 1 deliberately uses NO loop. The defect never needed one — a loop only
turned a wrong answer into a catastrophic one. Four loop-based repros failed to
separate the two causes; three straight-line assignments did it immediately.
If this pin ever regresses, TEST 1 is the one that localises it.

//@ run-pass
//@ expect-stdout-contains: PASS
//
// Native-stage mirror for the F1 Moufang/alternativity smoke. The original
// import-bearing program is parked under tests/madaros/ocssm_imported/.

fn embed_axis(hash: i64) -> i64 {
    let r: i64 = hash - (hash / 7) * 7
    return 1 + r
}

fn embed_into(hash: i64, out: &![f64; 8]) with Mut {
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < 8 {
        out[i as usize] = 0.0
        i = i + 1
    }
    out[0] = 0.6
    out[embed_axis(hash) as usize] = 0.8
}

fn oct_mul(a: &[f64; 8], b: &[f64; 8], out: &![f64; 8]) with Mut, Div, NonAssoc {
    var r0 = a[0] * b[0]
    r0 = r0 - a[1] * b[1]
    r0 = r0 - a[2] * b[2]
    r0 = r0 - a[3] * b[3]
    r0 = r0 - a[4] * b[4]
    r0 = r0 - a[5] * b[5]
    r0 = r0 - a[6] * b[6]
    r0 = r0 - a[7] * b[7]
    out[0] = r0

    var r1 = a[0] * b[1] + a[1] * b[0]
    r1 = r1 + a[2] * b[3] - a[3] * b[2]
    r1 = r1 + a[4] * b[5] - a[5] * b[4]
    r1 = r1 - a[6] * b[7] + a[7] * b[6]
    out[1] = r1

    var r2 = a[0] * b[2] + a[2] * b[0]
    r2 = r2 - a[1] * b[3] + a[3] * b[1]
    r2 = r2 + a[4] * b[6] - a[6] * b[4]
    r2 = r2 + a[5] * b[7] - a[7] * b[5]
    out[2] = r2

    var r3 = a[0] * b[3] + a[3] * b[0]
    r3 = r3 + a[1] * b[2] - a[2] * b[1]
    r3 = r3 + a[4] * b[7] - a[7] * b[4]
    r3 = r3 - a[5] * b[6] + a[6] * b[5]
    out[3] = r3

    var r4 = a[0] * b[4] + a[4] * b[0]
    r4 = r4 - a[1] * b[5] + a[5] * b[1]
    r4 = r4 - a[2] * b[6] + a[6] * b[2]
    r4 = r4 - a[3] * b[7] + a[7] * b[3]
    out[4] = r4

    var r5 = a[0] * b[5] + a[5] * b[0]
    r5 = r5 + a[1] * b[4] - a[4] * b[1]
    r5 = r5 - a[2] * b[7] + a[7] * b[2]
    r5 = r5 + a[3] * b[6] - a[6] * b[3]
    out[5] = r5

    var r6 = a[0] * b[6] + a[6] * b[0]
    r6 = r6 + a[1] * b[7] - a[7] * b[1]
    r6 = r6 + a[2] * b[4] - a[4] * b[2]
    r6 = r6 - a[3] * b[5] + a[5] * b[3]
    out[6] = r6

    var r7 = a[0] * b[7] + a[7] * b[0]
    r7 = r7 - a[1] * b[6] + a[6] * b[1]
    r7 = r7 + a[2] * b[5] - a[5] * b[2]
    r7 = r7 + a[3] * b[4] - a[4] * b[3]
    out[7] = r7
}

fn oct_associator(a: &[f64; 8], b: &[f64; 8], c: &[f64; 8], out: &![f64; 8]) with Mut, Div, NonAssoc {
    var ab: [f64; 8] = [0.0; 8]
    var ab_c: [f64; 8] = [0.0; 8]
    var bc: [f64; 8] = [0.0; 8]
    var a_bc: [f64; 8] = [0.0; 8]
    oct_mul(a, b, &!ab)
    oct_mul(&ab, c, &!ab_c)
    oct_mul(b, c, &!bc)
    oct_mul(a, &bc, &!a_bc)
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < 8 {
        out[i as usize] = ab_c[i as usize] - a_bc[i as usize]
        i = i + 1
    }
}

fn norm_sq(v: &[f64; 8]) -> f64 {
    return v[0]*v[0] + v[1]*v[1] + v[2]*v[2] + v[3]*v[3]
         + v[4]*v[4] + v[5]*v[5] + v[6]*v[6] + v[7]*v[7]
}

fn alt_stat_sq(x: &[f64; 8], y: &[f64; 8]) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic, NonAssoc {
    var assoc: [f64; 8] = [0.0; 8]
    oct_associator(x, x, y, &!assoc)
    let den_sq: f64 = norm_sq(x) * norm_sq(x) * norm_sq(y)
    if den_sq < 0.0000000000000001 { return 0.0 }
    return norm_sq(&assoc) / den_sq
}

fn main() -> i64 with IO, Mut, Div, Panic, NonAssoc {
    var hashes: [i64; 8] = [100, 200, 100, 300, 200, 400, 300, 500]
    var sum: f64 = 0.0
    var count: i64 = 0
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < 8 {
        var j: i64 = i + 1
        while j < 8 {
            if hashes[i as usize] == hashes[j as usize] {
                var x: [f64; 8] = [0.0; 8]
                var y: [f64; 8] = [0.0; 8]
                embed_into(hashes[i as usize], &!x)
                embed_into(701 + i + j, &!y)
                sum = sum + alt_stat_sq(&x, &y)
                count = count + 1
            }
            j = j + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    var ok: i64 = 1
    var stat_sq: f64 = 0.0
    if count > 0 { stat_sq = sum / (count as f64) }
    if count == 0 { ok = 0 }
    if stat_sq >= 0.000000000000000000000001 { ok = 0 }

    if ok == 1 { print("PASS\n") } else { print("FAIL\n") }
    return 0
}

Bug (native-v2 / Madaros codegen): the if-merge register was typed
flow-insensitively — the last linear ir_copy won — and an f64-literal else arm
(`else { 0.0 }`) lowers to IrLoadImm (int-flagged), so the merge result was
left untyped. A subsequent `acc_in + k` then took the SSE add (acc_in is a
genuine f64 param) but loaded the *unflagged* `k` operand via cvtsi2sd,
reinterpreting its IEEE-754 bits as an integer → garbage.
Fixed in self-hosted/ir/lower.sio: expr_result_is_float_ref now has an ExprIf
case (arms join), and lower_if_expr_ref marks the merge register float when the
if-expression is float. lean_single always compiled this correctly.
Both arms reachable: float condition (step_fcond) and int condition
(step_icond) — the latter proves the defect is the float *result* merge, not
the condition.

sqrt, floor and ceil via extern "C", under the default Madaros engine.
These three are the libm names this backend answers with a single hardware
instruction, so every row below is exact and none of them is allowed to be
off by an ulp: SQRTSD for sqrt, ROUNDSD mode 1 for floor, mode 2 for ceil.
The rows are chosen so that a WRONG implementation cannot pass by accident:
floor and ceil disagree on every non-integer input, so a stub that emitted
the same instruction for both, or that truncated toward zero for both,
fails on the negative rows. Truncation toward zero equals floor for
positive x and equals ceil for negative x -- checking only positive inputs
would not tell the two apart, which is why -2.5 is here.
sqrt(30.25) = 5.5 is not an integer, so a stub returning a fabricated 0,
or the argument unchanged, or an integer-truncated result, all fail.

On x86-64 System V ABI:
- Integer-returning C functions (i32/i64/bool) return in RAX.
- Float-returning C functions (f64) return in XMM0.
Sounio's internal convention carries all values (including f64) as
bit-patterns in RAX.  When we call an extern "C" fn that returns
an integer, RAX is already correct — no fixup is needed.
The bug was that strip_extern_blocks() discarded extern "C"
declarations entirely, causing callers to receive xor-eax-eax (0)
via the undefined-variable fallback, so pid was always 0.
The fix: strip_extern_blocks() now parses each extern "C" fn decl
and emits a Sounio stub that calls the correct platform mechanism
(syscall for integer-returning OS functions; native impl for math).
The stub returns its result in RAX — the Sounio calling convention —
so the return-register dispatch is always correct.

pow and tgamma reference vectors. GENERATED by
scripts/dev/gen_pow_tgamma_fixture.py from scripts/research/pow_tgamma_oracle.py.
Do not hand-edit: regenerate. A hand-copied bit pattern is a transcription
error in the one place where the test would certify it rather than catch it.
The reference is the ORACLE, decided against mpmath at 60 digits, and NOT
libm. glibc's tgamma returns 355687428096000.1 where 17! is the integer
355687428096000, and is 1 ulp off on 18!, 19!, 21! and 22! as well -- five
consecutive exactly-representable factorials, precisely the rows a fixture
should assert hardest. Asserting agreement with libm would fail a correct
implementation.
Tolerance is per row, from the design's own classification: rows with an
exactly representable answer are bit-exact, the rest carry the published
bound (pow <= 2 ulp, tgamma <= 5 ulp). Comparison is the integer distance
between bit patterns, which IS the ulp distance for two finite values of the
same sign; NaN rows assert NaN-ness instead, since IEEE-754 leaves a
generated NaN's sign and payload unspecified.

comments: requires: madaros because lean_single carries its OWN copy of the decimal
conversion, inside lean_single.sio, still the pre-#1626 one -- it gets five
of these ten wrong. The suite's stage2 binary is built by lean_single, so
without this guard the test is a false red. Porting the bignum path there is
a separate change: it needs its own seed re-derivation. Filed as follow-up.
#1626: decimal -> binary64 must be correctly rounded, not merely close.
The original conversion accumulated `frac = frac * 0.1`, and 0.1 is not
representable, so every digit compounded a rounding: 32 of 91 realistic
literals were wrong. Exact fast paths took that to 4, and the bignum slow
path takes it to 0 -- measured at 0 wrong across 920 random literals
spanning 1e-320 to 1e300, against 359 wrong on the pre-fix compiler.
Every literal below is one that a shortcut got wrong at some point in that
sequence. Keep them: each one is a different failure mode, and they are
cheap insurance against the next person reaching for a shortcut.
0.99999999            one ULP high; this is what made log look like it
had a 2^-53 residual, since ulp(1.0)/1.0 IS 2^-53
944.6810951079374     16 significant digits -- trimming the significand
to 2^53 threw away a digit it actually carries
118.06577825496211    17 digits; f64 accumulation stops at 2^53
1.602176634e-19       |exponent| > 22, outside the exact power-of-ten window
1e300 / 1e-300        chunked scaling cost one rounding per chunk
610e-315              SUBNORMAL: extracting 53 bits and scaling down
rounds twice, because binary64 loses precision
gradually below 2^-1022
Compared against bit patterns from CPython. Kept short on purpose: a file
with ~150 such comparisons hits a separate Madaros miscompile and reports
false failures, which cost a measurement pass to notice.

The Furey one-generation construction (ℂ⊗𝕆 → Cℓ(6)): left-mult L_a on the octonion (8-dim), ladder
operators α_i = ½(−L_{a_i} + i L_{b_i}) for pairs (1,2),(3,4),(5,6). Scaling by 2 gives Gaussian-integer
matrices M_i = 2α_i = −L_{a_i} + i L_{b_i}. This test certifies:

This EXECUTES an established result (C. Furey, "Standard model physics from an algebra?", and the Dixon/Furey C(x)O program): the complex octonions C(x)O carry a fermionic ladder algebra of three. description: FRENTE B, vector 4/3 Part A — Sounio reproduces Furey's octonion -> one Standard-Model generation. This EXECUTES an established result (C. Furey, "Standard model physics from an algebra?", and the Dixon/Furey C(x)O program): the complex octonions C(x)O carry a fermionic ladder algebra of three
comments: FRENTE B, vector 4/3 Part A — Sounio reproduces Furey's octonion -> one Standard-Model generation.
This EXECUTES an established result (C. Furey, "Standard model physics from an algebra?", and the
Dixon/Furey C(x)O program): the complex octonions C(x)O carry a fermionic ladder algebra of three
modes whose number operator gives the electric charges of exactly one generation of quarks + leptons,
with the x3 multiplicities of SU(3) colour. We build it EXACTLY over the Gaussian integers Z[i].
Left-multiplication operators (8x8 integer matrices) over Sounio's octonion convention (cd_sigma at
bits=3): for the unit e_a, L_a has L_a[a^b][b] = cd_sigma(a,b,3) in column b (e_a * e_b = sign*e_{a^b}).
Furey's ladder operators are alpha_i = 1/2(-L_{a_i} + i L_{b_i}) for the pairs
(a_1,b_1),(a_2,b_2),(a_3,b_3) = (1,2),(3,4),(5,6)   [relative to Sounio's cd_sigma sign convention].
To stay in exact integers we use A_i = 2*alpha_i, the complex 8x8 matrix with real part -L_{a_i} and
imaginary part L_{b_i}. A complex matrix is TWO int arrays (Re, Im), 64 entries row-major each.
Adjoint A^dag = conjugate-transpose = (Re^T, -Im^T). Complex matmul
(Xr+iXi)(Yr+iYi) = (XrYr - XiYi) + i(XrYi + XiYr).
CLAIM 1 (the headline, exact over Z[i]): the three A_i close a fermionic ladder algebra —
{A_i, A_j}      = 0                (all 9 pairs, both Re and Im zero)
{A_i, A_j^dag}  = 4*delta_ij * I   (Re = 4*I if i==j else 0; Im zero)
(the factor 4 is because A = 2*alpha; alpha itself gives delta_ij). 18 anticommutator relations.
CLAIM 2 (charge spectrum, combinatorial given Claim 1): the fermionic Fock space of the 3 modes has
occupation-number multiplicities C(3,n) = {0:1, 1:3, 2:3, 3:1}, so the electric charge Q = N/3 takes
the values {0, 1/3, 2/3, 1} with those multiplicities (the x3 = SU(3) colour triplets). The conjugate
ideal supplies {0, -1/3, -2/3, -1} -> the full 16-state generation. We emit Q*3 -> multiplicity.
Decidable integer arithmetic, no float. SELF-CONTAINED (cd_sigma copied verbatim; no stdlib import).
Cross-verified vs scripts/research/furey_octonion_oracle.py by scripts/ci/furey_octonion_gate.sh and
by formal/lean4/SounioFureyOctonion.lean (native_decide).

`1` seven times. Madaros was already correct.
Root cause: emit_global_inits_x86 treated every `[...]` after `=` as the
REPEAT form `[V; N]`. On a list it parsed `1` as V, never found the `;`, and
rep-stosq`d that one value across all N slots. The local declaration path had
gated on array_init_is_repeat since it was written; only the two global
emitters had not.

collapsed to element 0 sums to 7, and a sum-based assertion would also pass on
`[7,0,0,0,0,0,0]`. The bug it is guarding is precisely a wrong DISTRIBUTION.
The i8 array pins the esiz == 1 store, which takes the byte branch, and the
SHORT list pins that a list shorter than the declared length leaves the tail
on its BSS zero rather than running off the end of the array.

description: sensitivity_of() implemented via β⁴ shadow buffer in lean_single.sio THE SURPRISE: gradient descent in Sounio. β⁴'s per-channel sensitivity buffer stores ∂y/∂x_k — literally, the
comments: sensitivity_of() implemented via β⁴ shadow buffer in lean_single.sio
THE SURPRISE: gradient descent in Sounio.
β⁴'s per-channel sensitivity buffer stores ∂y/∂x_k — literally, the
gradient of y with respect to each uncertain input x_k, computed by
the compiler at emit-time via forward-mode automatic differentiation.
We expose this via the new `sensitivity_of(y, k)` builtin. That turns
Sounio — a language originally designed for epistemic typed computing —
into an automatic-differentiation language.
To prove it: minimize L(x) = (x − 3)² by gradient descent, using the
compiler's sensitivity as the gradient. No external library. No manual
derivative. The compiler knows dL/dx because it computed it while
emitting the code.
Starting x = 0. Learning rate 0.1. 30 iterations.
Expected: x → 3.0, L → 0.

use graphics::drawing::{color_red, color_green, color_blue, color_white, color_black}
use graphics::svg::{svg_line_plot, svg_scatter_plot, svg_heatmap_plot, svg_epistemic_band_plot}

fn main() -> i64 with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    var xs: [f64; 256] = [0.0; 256]
    var ys: [f64; 256] = [0.0; 256]
    xs[0] = 0.0
    ys[0] = 0.0
    xs[1] = 1.0
    ys[1] = 1.0
    print("<!-- line -->\n")
    svg_line_plot(&xs, &ys, 2, 64, 64, 8, color_red(), color_white(), color_black())
    print("<!-- scatter -->\n")
    svg_scatter_plot(&xs, &ys, 2, 64, 64, 8, color_blue(), color_white(), color_black())

    var data: [f64; 4096] = [0.0; 4096]
    data[0] = 0.0
    data[1] = 1.0
    data[2] = 0.5
    data[3] = 0.25
    print("<!-- heatmap -->\n")
    svg_heatmap_plot(&data, 2, 2, 64, 64, 8, color_white(), color_black())

    var center: [f64; 256] = [0.0; 256]
    var lower: [f64; 256] = [0.0; 256]
    var upper: [f64; 256] = [0.0; 256]
    center[0] = 0.5
    lower[0] = 0.25
    upper[0] = 0.75
    center[1] = 0.5
    lower[1] = 0.25
    upper[1] = 0.75
    print("<!-- epistemic -->\n")
    svg_epistemic_band_plot(&xs, &center, &lower, &upper, 2, 64, 64, 8, color_red(), color_green(), color_white(), color_black())
    0
}

shown to be NON-MONOMIAL. This decisively answers the arc's question: the fermion family symmetry is
NOT a signed permutation, so it lies OUTSIDE the zero-divisor monomial-168 — there is no bridge from
the ZD-168 to fermion generations. Erratum E1 vindicated, now with the family generator explicit.
From Gresnigt arXiv:2306.13098 §5, eq (70)-(76): the order-3 family automorphism ψ acts as a 120°
rotation in each plane {e_i, e_{i+8}} (i=1..7), fixing e_0, e_8:
The √3 makes ψ irrational — NON-MONOMIAL. We work over ℤ[√3] by scaling: 2ψ has integer coefficients
in the basis {1, √3}. A number is (p, q) = p + q√3; (p+q√3)(r+s√3) = (pr+3qs) + (ps+qr)√3.
Certified over ℤ[√3]:
(1) ψ is a genuine sedenion automorphism: (2ψ)(e_j)·(2ψ)(e_k) = 2·σ(j,k)·(2ψ)(e_{j⊕k}), all 256 pairs;
(2) ψ has order 3: (2ψ)³(e_i) = 8·e_i;
(3) ψ is NON-MONOMIAL: some (2ψ)(e_j) has a nonzero √3 component;
(4) ψ maps the gen-1 ladder A†_1=(e₁+ie₅+e₉+ie₁₃) to the gen-2 ladder B†_1 (Gresnigt eq 70-76,
a=(√3−1)/2, b=(−√3−1)/2), confirming this IS his family generator: 2ψ(A†_1 real=e₁+e₉) gives
(√3−1)e₁ + (−√3−1)e₉ = 2b₁; likewise the imaginary part.
(Frame-relative mechanism, certified in the Lean/oracle legs: the monomial φ=(e₁e₂e₃)(e₅e₆e₇)... —
a color-triplet Weyl-S₃ element — commutes with the gen-1 number operator N, while ψ carries N to the
gen-2 operator. See furey_charge_g2.md (#707) for the complementary 8-dim frame; the physically
relevant charge is the 16-dim Gresnigt one. This brick delivers the family generator #707 left open.)
Decidable ℤ[√3] arithmetic, no float. SELF-CONTAINED. Cross-verified vs the oracle + Lean.

From Gresnigt arXiv:2306.13098 §4.3 (eq 47-55): the sedenion automorphism group is Aut(𝕊)=G₂×S₃, with
the family S₃ = ⟨ψ, ϵ⟩ generated by
ψ (order 3, eq 51-54): 120° rotation in each {e_i,e_{i+8}} plane (i=1..7), fixing e₀,e₈ — NON-MONOMIAL
(uses √3), and the ONLY automorphism that mixes original octonion units e_i (i≤7) with the new
sedenion units e_{i+8};
ϵ (order 2, eq 55/49): ϵ(e_i)=e_i for i≤7, ϵ(e_i)=−e_i for i≥8 — a MONOMIAL (diagonal-sign) involution.
satisfying ϵ²=ψ³=1, ϵψ=ψ²ϵ (an S₃).  The color-triplet Weyl element φ=(e₁e₂e₃)(e₅e₆e₇)(e₉e₁₀e₁₁)(e₁₃e₁₄e₁₅)
∈ G₂ commutes with BOTH family generators — executing color ⟂ family (the direct product).
Certified (over ℤ[√3]; 2ψ is scaled to integer coefficients in {1,√3}):
EPS_AUTO   : ϵ is a genuine sedenion automorphism;
S3_REL     : ϵ∘ψ = ψ²∘ϵ  (the defining S₃ braid relation; ϵ²=ψ³=1 hold by construction/#708);
COMM_PHI_PSI : [φ, ψ] = 0   ┐ color-Weyl φ commutes with the whole family S₃
COMM_PHI_EPS : [φ, ϵ] = 0   ┘ ⟹ G₂ and S₃ are commuting (direct) factors — Aut(𝕊)=G₂×S₃, executed;
PSI_NONMONO: ψ is non-monomial (√3) — the generation-cycling map is rotational, outside the ZD-168;
EPS_MONO   : ϵ is monomial (so the family S₃ is not *entirely* non-monomial — but its generation-
cycling element ψ is, which is what makes the ZD-168 carry no generation structure);
ONLY_PSI_MIXES: only ψ mixes octonion (≤7) and new (≥8) units; ϵ and φ do not.
HONEST NOTE. This does not reprove all of Brown's theorem (that Aut(𝕊) is EXACTLY G₂×S₃ with nothing
more); it certifies that ψ, ϵ are the stated automorphisms, generate an S₃, and commute with the color
element φ ∈ G₂ — the commuting-factors structure the "no bridge" conclusion uses. Erratum E1 and #708
stand: the generation symmetry ψ is rotational, hence not in the zero-divisor monomial-168.
Decidable ℤ[√3] / integer arithmetic, no float. SELF-CONTAINED. Cross-verified vs the oracle + Lean.

Week-3 unioned every argument's channel set into the return topology
(conservative upper bound).  For
fn proj_a(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 { a }
let r = proj_a(k0.value, k1.value)
week-3 left EXPR_CH_SET(r) = {ch0, ch1} even though the body reads
only its first parameter.  Week-4 introduces body-level precision:
the compiler walks the callee's return expression, records the set
of parameter indices it actually depends on into FN_USED_PARAMS[fi],
and at each call site unions only those B9_ARG_CH_SET slots.  The
declared channel set becomes EXPR_CH_SET(r) = {ch0} — tight.
This test is the positive canary: the hessian query that remains
inside the tightened set (H_{0,0}) still type-checks and runs.  The
counterpart compile-fail test (gtt_body_precision_unused_param_refused)
verifies that the out-of-topology query (H_{1,1}) is now refused.
my_sum / my_square from the week-3 regression continue to type-check
under body-precision: my_sum's body references both params (union of
operand topologies = union of both args); my_square uses only one
arg (and only has one), so the tightened set matches what week-3
happened to produce by accident.

instruction: Write a Sounio run-pass example named `gtt_if_arm_union`. Gradient Topology Types (GTT) — β⁹ week-6 stage-2 regression (if-arm union). description: Gradient Topology Types (GTT) — β⁹ week-6 stage-2 regression (if-arm union). Before this fix, `compile_primary`'s if-expression path (line ~15889) compiled both arms but did NOT propagate EXPR_CH_SET through them —
comments: Gradient Topology Types (GTT) — β⁹ week-6 stage-2 regression (if-arm union).
Before this fix, `compile_primary`'s if-expression path (line ~15889)
compiled both arms but did NOT propagate EXPR_CH_SET through them —
each arm's compilation overwrote EXPR_CH_SET, so the result carried
only the last-compiled arm's topology (usually the else arm).
Concretely, for
let k0 = measure(...)
let k1 = measure(...)
let r = if flag { k0.value } else { k1.value }
hessian_of(r, 0, 0)
pre-fix left EXPR_CH_SET = {ch1} (else arm's), and the query
H_{0,0} was REFUSED at type-check because channel 0 was not in the
set — a real soundness hole.
Post-fix: EXPR_CH_SET = cond_ch_set | then_ch_set | else_ch_set.
Both H_{0,0} and H_{1,1} queries are accepted; the runtime value
depends on which arm actually ran (shadow channels aren't
path-sensitive at Phase-1 level, but topology tracking is now
correctly a conservative upper bound).
The theorem this commit catches up to: `Typing.tIf` in
formal/GradientTopology.lean §3 concludes at `Sc ∪ (S1 ∪ S2)`, which
`gtt_sound` proves is a sound runtime-footprint upper bound.

description: Gradient Topology Types (GTT) — β⁹ week-9 indirect-call regression. Open item #2 from formal/GradientTopology.lean §7c: closure / fn-ref indirect calls were leaking the last `compile_or()` arg's
comments: Gradient Topology Types (GTT) — β⁹ week-9 indirect-call regression.
Open item #2 from formal/GradientTopology.lean §7c: closure / fn-ref
indirect calls were leaking the last `compile_or()` arg's
EXPR_CH_SET / EXPR_PARAM_USED unchanged.  A 2-arg fn-ref dispatched
indirectly with args carrying ch[0] and ch[1] would leave EXPR_CH_SET
= {ch1}, and `hessian_of(f(x,y), 0, 1)` would be REFUSED at type-check
for the wrong reason (channel 0 missing) — silently masking the
soundness hole.
Week-9 unions B9_ARG_CH_SET[0..min(argc,16)] for indirect calls
(no body precision possible — callee body is unknown), with the
same saturating widen at argc ≥ 16 as week-8 stage 2.  This test
pins down acceptance of the (0,1) and (1,0) cross-pairs.
Runtime value is silent zero (inter-procedural shadow propagation
is orthogonal to topology — see gtt_interprocedural_topology.sio).
The point is type-check acceptance.

description: Gradient Topology Types (GTT) — β⁹ week-3 regression (inter-procedural). Week-2 tracked channel topology through let-bindings, additive/ multiplicative ops, and two-arg builtins (atan2, pow).  It did NOT
comments: Gradient Topology Types (GTT) — β⁹ week-3 regression (inter-procedural).
Week-2 tracked channel topology through let-bindings, additive/
multiplicative ops, and two-arg builtins (atan2, pow).  It did NOT
union topology across user-defined function calls — the return
inherited only the *last* argument's channel set.
Concretely, for
fn my_sum(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 { a + b }
let x = k0.value   // channel 0
let y = k1.value   // channel 1
hessian_of(my_sum(x, y), 0, 1)
week-2 left EXPR_CH_SET = {ch1} (only y's topology), and the query
H_{0,1} was REFUSED at type-check because channel 0 was not in the set.
Week-3 unions the channel sets of every argument into the return
topology (conservative upper bound, matching the atan2/pow discipline).
The same program now type-checks.  The runtime value is 0.0 because
inter-procedural SSHADOW propagation is not yet wired — topology
tracking and shadow tracking are orthogonal concerns.  This test
asserts that the type checker accepts the query; the shadow pipeline
is covered by epistemic_hessian_*.
Single-arg fns (my_square below) were correct by accident pre-fix and
continue to work — union of one set is itself.

None    => k1.value,   // channel 1
hessian_of(r, 0, 0)
pre-fix left EXPR_CH_SET = {ch1} (last-compiled arm's), and H_{0,0}

description: Gradient Topology Types (GTT) — β⁹ week-8 regression (n-ary surface). Week-3 unioned channel topology across binary user-fn calls (gtt_interprocedural_topology.sio).  Week-4 added body-precision
comments: Gradient Topology Types (GTT) — β⁹ week-8 regression (n-ary surface).
Week-3 unioned channel topology across binary user-fn calls
(gtt_interprocedural_topology.sio).  Week-4 added body-precision
filtering via FN_USED_PARAMS.  Week-5 introduced Lean's Expr.callN
+ gtt_sound_body_callN soundness.  The compiler-side variadic
iteration over B9_ARG_CH_SET[16] has been live since week-3, but
was only validated at arity 2.  This test locks in arities 3..5
to prove the union scales smoothly across the per-arg slot table.
Concretely, for
fn my_sum3(a, b, c) -> f64 { a + b + c }
let x = k0.value   // channel 0
let y = k1.value   // channel 1
let z = k2.value   // channel 2
hessian_of(my_sum3(x, y, z), 0, 2)
pre-week-3 would have leaked only z's topology ({ch2}); the (0, 2)
query would have refused on missing channel 0.  Week-3's variadic
union over B9_ARG_CH_SET emits {ch0, ch1, ch2}, so every cross-pair
query type-checks.  This test verifies the (0,1), (0,2), (1,2)
triangle for arity 3, and analogous coverage for arity 4 and 5.

description: Gradient Topology Types (GTT) — β⁹ week-10 regression (recursion). Recursion is already handled by the week-3 conservative union: at each call site, B9_ARG_CH_SET accumulates all argument channel sets, and the
comments: Gradient Topology Types (GTT) — β⁹ week-10 regression (recursion).
Recursion is already handled by the week-3 conservative union: at each
call site, B9_ARG_CH_SET accumulates all argument channel sets, and the
return value's EXPR_CH_SET is the union.  For a recursive call like
fn depth_sum(x: f64, n: i64) -> f64 { if n == 0 { x } else { depth_sum(x, n-1) } }
the call site unions the argument topology (ch0) into the return, so
`hessian_of(depth_sum(k0.value, 3), 0, 0)` is correctly accepted.
This test is the positive canary confirming recursion topology is sound.

comments: gum_independence_required.sio

Eq. (10) — plain quadrature — is the rho = 0 special case, not the general law.

shared drivers (time of day, activity) — so the unsafe direction is the

`prescribe_haloperidol` is annotated `with Confidence(750)`. Per the compiler's
EpistemicComplete gate, every expression inside the body must carry compile-time
confidence ≥ 750/1000.
`measure(40.0, uncertainty: 1.6)` yields confidence = 1 − 1.6/40.0 = 0.96
= 960/1000, which EXCEEDS the 750 threshold. The compiler emits binary code.
Clinical narrative: post-CYP2D6 genotyping with activity score confirms NM
phenotype. The star-allele call (e.g., *1/*1) reduces CL uncertainty to ±4%
(measurement CV), well above the Confidence(750) threshold. The program
compiles — prescribing is authorised.

instruction: Write a Sounio run-pass example named `hypercomplex_convention_crosscheck`. Canonical hypercomplex convention oracle (Convention X = cd_sigma / XOR indexing). This test PINS the canonical octonion/sedenion multiplication convention as executable truth: e_i·e_j = σ(i,j)·e_{i⊕j}, where σ is the recursive Cayley–Dickson 2-cocycle `cd_sigma`. description: Canonical hypercomplex convention oracle (Convention X = cd_sigma / XOR indexing). This test PINS the canonical octonion/sedenion multiplication convention as executable truth: e_i·e_j = σ(i,j)·e_{i⊕j}, where σ is the recursive Cayley–Dickson 2-cocycle `cd_sigma`
comments: Canonical hypercomplex convention oracle (Convention X = cd_sigma / XOR indexing).
This test PINS the canonical octonion/sedenion multiplication convention as executable truth:
e_i·e_j = σ(i,j)·e_{i⊕j}, where σ is the recursive Cayley–Dickson 2-cocycle `cd_sigma`
(Albuquerque–Majid; the same sign function in stdlib/algebra/octonion.sio and
stdlib/algebra/cayley_dickson.sio). It is the reference every oct_mul/sed_mul implementation must
match — see stdlib/algebra/README.md ("Multiplication convention").
Asserted invariants:
* e_i² = −1                       (octonion i=1..7, sedenion i=1..15)
* e1·e2 = +e3, e2·e5 = +e7        (canonical basis products)
* octonion norm-multiplicativity  ‖xy‖² = ‖x‖²‖y‖²  (octonions are a normed division algebra)
* canonical sedenion zero-divisor (e3+e10)·(e6−e15) = 0  (exactly)
* octonion non-associativity present (associator ≠ 0 for some basis triple)
Single-module (cd_sigma inlined) to avoid the multimodule thin-link defect (#921).
By-value array params + array return (Madaros miscompiles multiple `&[f64;N]` ref params).

semantics for >>, /, %. If a refactor accidentally makes signed operands go
through the unsigned path, this fixture detects it.
Signed semantics (truncation toward zero; sign of quotient follows dividend):
- -7_i64 / 2 = -3 (truncate toward zero, not floor)
- -7_i64 % 2 = -1 (sign matches dividend)
- -1_i64 >> 1 = -1 (arithmetic shift keeps sign)
- -8_i64 >> 1 = -4 (arithmetic shift, sign-preserving)
- IntMin / -1 is UB; we do not test it (avoid divide exception).

instruction: Write a Sounio run-pass example named `index_set_value_survives_dce`. #1682: -O deleted the register holding the VALUE of an indexed store. IrIndexSet has three register operands -- base, index, value -- but IrInstr has only src1/src2, so ir_index_set parks the value in `imm_i64`. An immediate. It should compile and run successfully. Expected stdout: a1=5 a2=9 b0=1 b3=4
description: #1682: -O deleted the register holding the VALUE of an indexed store. IrIndexSet has three register operands -- base, index, value -- but IrInstr has only src1/src2, so ir_index_set parks the value in `imm_i64`. An immediate
comments: #1682: -O deleted the register holding the VALUE of an indexed store.
IrIndexSet has three register operands -- base, index, value -- but IrInstr
has only src1/src2, so ir_index_set parks the value in `imm_i64`. An immediate
slot holding a register is exactly what a liveness scan does not look at, and
ocp_mfi_dce_once scanned src1/src2 only. The load_imm defining the stored
value was therefore removed as dead.
Before the fix, under -O: a1=0 a2=0 b0=0 b3=0.
Deliberately uses a ZERO-fill initialiser. A non-zero fill (`[7; 4]`) lowers
to a fill loop, and that loop hangs under -O on account of a SEPARATE, still
open defect (#1667, propagation across block boundaries) -- so a test written
that way would time out rather than fail, and would be testing two things at
once. Zero fill emits no loop, which isolates this defect exactly.
Only meaningful WITH -O; without it the pass does not run and this passes
vacuously.

comments: Engine-gated, not silenced. The CI suite runs souc-stage2 -- the lean_single
self-host output, set as SOUNIO_TEST_SOUC_BIN in .github/workflows/ci.yml --

`on` is lexed into TokenKind::On by self-hosted/parser/parser.sio for the

lexical class at all, so before this fixture the two engines disagreed about
whether `on` is a valid identifier: this file parse-failed under Madaros and
compiled clean under lean_single.

viz/ir.sio, theorem/cdcl.sio -- and one of them blocks a chain: surface.sio
is imported by canvas_ext, which is imported by renderer3d, which is imported
by viz/ir, so EVERY viz_* test sat behind a single file that would not parse.
The fix is contextual, not a rename: TokenKind::On joins
tk_is_contextual_ident, so the three identifier positions accept it while the
token kind and the Contest parse are untouched.

instruction: Write a Sounio run-pass example named `knightian_dark_matter`. Knightian Uncertainty Demo: Dark Matter Candidates Frank Knight (1921) distinguished: Risk        = unknown outcome, known probability distribution. It should compile and run successfully. description: Knightian Uncertainty Demo: Dark Matter Candidates Frank Knight (1921) distinguished: Risk        = unknown outcome, known probability distribution
comments: Knightian Uncertainty Demo: Dark Matter Candidates
Frank Knight (1921) distinguished:
Risk        = unknown outcome, known probability distribution
Uncertainty = unknown outcome, unknown distribution (ε=⊥)
Dark matter is the canonical example of Knightian uncertainty:
- We know it exists (gravitational effects are real)
- We have zero confidence in ANY model class: WIMPs, axions,
primordial black holes, modified gravity — all have been ruled out
or are severely constrained. The hypothesis SPACE is unknown.
This is not "low confidence." This is "undefined confidence."
ε=0.0 means "known to be wrong." ε=⊥ means "model space unknown."
The Knightian distinction requires different decision theory:
Risk:        Bayesian updating, expected utility maximization
Uncertainty: Maximin strategies, robust optimization
In Sounio: KnightianMode::Undefined propagates through computation.
Any function of ε=⊥ must return ε=⊥.
The distinction is enforced by the type system, not by convention.

instruction: Write a Sounio run-pass example named `knowledge_layout_shadows_user_field_name`. A user struct field named `value` was silently clobbered by its sibling. `ir_register_knowledge_layout` preseeds a synthetic `Knowledge` layout — value@0, variance@1, confidence@2 — as entry 0 of the struct layout table,. It should compile and run successfully. Expected stdout: oid=85,29 value=170,187 variance=7 confidence=9
description: A user struct field named `value` was silently clobbered by its sibling. `ir_register_knowledge_layout` preseeds a synthetic `Knowledge` layout — value@0, variance@1, confidence@2 — as entry 0 of the struct layout table,
comments: A user struct field named `value` was silently clobbered by its sibling.
`ir_register_knowledge_layout` preseeds a synthetic `Knowledge` layout —
value@0, variance@1, confidence@2 — as entry 0 of the struct layout table,
before any user struct is registered. `field_idx_from_name_simple` resolves a
field *name* to a slot by scanning the whole table in order and taking the
first hit in any struct, and that path is what runs whenever the base is not
a typed local: `arr[i].f` reaches it because array locals record a length but
no element type.
So `ext[0].value` resolved to Knowledge's slot 0 — the same slot as `oid` —
and `ext[0].value = val_buf` overwrote the `oid` written just before it. Both
reads then went to slot 0 too, so `value` read back correct while `oid`
returned `value`'s bytes: a silent wrong answer at rc=0, with no diagnostic.
The trigger was the identifier, not the shape. The same program with the
field named `val` was always correct, at any struct size, array length or
index form — which is why size- and index-threshold hypotheses all died.
Guard all three preseeded names. Anything reading its sibling's data here
means the synthetic layout is shadowing user layouts again.
Honest scope: CI runs this suite under souc-stage2, which never carried the
defect, so this file is green either way there — it is the readable witness,
not the guard. The discriminating gate is the `knowledge_field_shadow` case
in tests/madaros/source_to_elf/manifest.tsv, which compiles with Madaros and
was measured red before this fix and green after.

instruction: Write a Sounio run-pass example named `knowledge_octonion_inner`. M1 functor F foundation — Knowledge<Octonion> as a single epistemic capsule. Existing run-pass `knowledge_octonion_structure.sio` carries uncertainty on each of the eight octonion *components* (`Knowledge<f64>` × 8). This test. It should compile and run successfully.
description: M1 functor F foundation — Knowledge<Octonion> as a single epistemic capsule. Existing run-pass `knowledge_octonion_structure.sio` carries uncertainty on each of the eight octonion *components* (`Knowledge<f64>` × 8). This test
comments: M1 functor F foundation — Knowledge<Octonion> as a single epistemic capsule.
Existing run-pass `knowledge_octonion_structure.sio` carries uncertainty on
each of the eight octonion *components* (`Knowledge<f64>` × 8). This test
pins the dual idiom that the homology-functor plan (project_octonion_homology_functor)
requires: a single `Knowledge<T>` wrapping the whole struct.
What it proves about the compiler today:
1. Parser accepts `Knowledge<Octonion>` (struct as inner type, not just f64/i64).
2. Type-checker accepts the `Knowledge { value: octonion_literal }` construction.
3. `.value` projection through a struct inner returns the struct.
4. Composing two `Knowledge<Octonion>` values via a hand-written multiplier
that does the algebra on the underlying `Octonion` (not on the Knowledge
capsule directly) lowers to ELF and runs.
What it does NOT claim: arithmetic operators (+ - * /) on `Knowledge<Octonion>`
directly — the codegen at lean_single.sio:6796 legitimately rejects struct
inner types for those operators because GUM variance propagation requires a
scalar value channel. Composition lives in user-space algebra (oct_mul) and
re-wraps via `Knowledge { value: ... }`. That is the F functor's intended shape.

instruction: Write a Sounio run-pass example named `knowledge_octonion_structure`. variance_of() implemented via β⁴ shadow buffer in lean_single.sio β-2: Knowledge<Octonion<f64>> — first GUM variance through octonion multiplication. description: variance_of() implemented via β⁴ shadow buffer in lean_single.sio β-2: Knowledge<Octonion<f64>> — first GUM variance through octonion multiplication. Demonstrates the Fano-plane structure tensor and non-commutativity via variance
comments: variance_of() implemented via β⁴ shadow buffer in lean_single.sio
β-2: Knowledge<Octonion<f64>> — first GUM variance through octonion multiplication.
Demonstrates the Fano-plane structure tensor and non-commutativity via variance
asymmetry. Based on Baez "The Octonions" Bull. AMS 39 (2002).
Fano-plane convention (positive orientation):
Reverse order -> negated. e_i*e_i = -1. e_0 = 1.
Product is computed inline (no 16-param helper) because narrow param lists are
preferred by the self-hosted compiler. Variance is sampled from c0 and d0
(first components of a*b and b*a) to avoid the 3-chain x 3-stage overflow path.

instruction: Write a Sounio run-pass example named `knowledge_quaternion_mekf`. Task: beta-1 (Knowledge<Quaternion<f64>> with MEKF-style tangent-space cov) β-1: Knowledge<Quaternion<f64>> demonstration. Compares naive ambient GUM (quaternion as 4 packed Knowledge<f64> on R^4). It should compile and run successfully.
description: Task: beta-1 (Knowledge<Quaternion<f64>> with MEKF-style tangent-space cov) β-1: Knowledge<Quaternion<f64>> demonstration. Compares naive ambient GUM (quaternion as 4 packed Knowledge<f64> on R^4)
comments: Task: beta-1 (Knowledge<Quaternion<f64>> with MEKF-style tangent-space cov)
β-1: Knowledge<Quaternion<f64>> demonstration.
Compares naive ambient GUM (quaternion as 4 packed Knowledge<f64> on R^4)
against the spirit of MEKF/LIEKF: a nominal unit quaternion with a
tangent-space (so(3)) error covariance. The former wastes a degree of
freedom on the unit-norm constraint and couples unrelated directions; the
latter tracks uncertainty in the 3-DoF small-angle error.
Witness: non-commutativity of the Hamilton product. The mean obeys
|q1*q2| = |q2*q1| = |q1||q2| (composition), but the GUM variance on the
vector components is NOT symmetric under order reversal, because the
partial derivatives of (w,x,y,z) = q1*q2 w.r.t. each input component are
a function of the OTHER operand, which differs between q1*q2 and q2*q1.
References:
- Markley, F.L. "Attitude Error Representations for Kalman Filtering"
J. Guidance, Control, and Dynamics 26(2), 2003. (MEKF)
- Barrau, A.; Bonnabel, S. "The Invariant Extended Kalman Filter as
a Stable Observer" IEEE TAC 62(4), 2017. (LIEKF)
- Shuster, M.D. "A Survey of Attitude Representations" J. Astro. Sci.
Why naive ambient GUM fails for rotations:
- q lives on S^3 in R^4 (unit-norm constraint w^2+x^2+y^2+z^2 = 1).
- Packing 4 independent Knowledge<f64> ignores the constraint; the
covariance ellipsoid leaks off the manifold.
- MEKF encodes uncertainty as dtheta in R^3 (so(3)), so P is 3x3
and stays on the tangent space. Here we mimic that by tracking
variance only on the 3 vector components (x,y,z) of the *error*
quaternion, treating w~=1 as the deterministic nominal.

a chi-squared statistic comparing observed vs. expected event counts.

instruction: Write a Sounio run-pass example named `long_string_literal_call_arg`. Regression test (segfault landmine, discovered via PR #2058): A string literal passed as a function-call argument is embedded directly in the generated code with a "jmp over the bytes, then lea rax back at. It should compile and run successfully.
description: Regression test (segfault landmine, discovered via PR #2058): A string literal passed as a function-call argument is embedded directly in the generated code with a "jmp over the bytes, then lea rax back at
comments: Regression test (segfault landmine, discovered via PR #2058):
A string literal passed as a function-call argument is embedded directly
in the generated code with a "jmp over the bytes, then lea rax back at
them" trick. The x86-64 codegen used a rel8 (single signed byte, -128..127)
displacement for that skip jump. Any literal whose decoded content was
>= 127 bytes made the skip distance overflow the byte, wrapping negative
and sending execution backward into unrelated, already-emitted code --
corrupting whatever ran next. The callee was never reached; the crash hit
while the *caller* was still setting up the argument.
This exercises a literal well past that threshold (~200 bytes) as a call
argument, and checks the callee receives the exact content -- not just
that the process survives.
