instruction: Write a Sounio run-pass example named `madaros_array_repeat_aggregate_distinct`. Gated behind `requires: madaros`: CI's full-test-suite runs souc-stage2 (lean_single), which has its OWN, separate defect on the nested-array cases exercised here -- it returns `999` for [[9;2];3] and `0` for the 3-level. It should compile and run successfully. Expected stdout: ARRAY_REPEAT_DISTINCT OK
description: Gated behind `requires: madaros`: CI's full-test-suite runs souc-stage2 (lean_single), which has its OWN, separate defect on the nested-array cases exercised here -- it returns `999` for [[9;2];3] and `0` for the 3-level
comments: Gated behind `requires: madaros`: CI's full-test-suite runs souc-stage2
(lean_single), which has its OWN, separate defect on the nested-array cases
exercised here -- it returns `999` for [[9;2];3] and `0` for the 3-level
case, dropping the writes entirely. That is not what this test is about, and
letting it fail there would pin an unrelated bug. This test asserts the
modular Madaros contract and runs on the madaros gate.
Regression: `[Aggregate; N]` repeat literals must allocate N DISTINCT objects.
Array slots are 8-byte boxed pointers (ir/lower.sio `aggregate_storage_bytes`
= elem_count * 8), so an aggregate element is a POINTER. Before the fix,
`lower_array_repeat_literal_ref` lowered the element expression once and
`lower_array_repeat_fill` stored that single pointer into every slot: all N
elements aliased ONE object, and a write through element i was observable
through every other element. Explicit-list literals were unaffected
(`lower_array_elems_ref` lowers per element), as were scalars.
`lower_array_repeat_fill_distinct` now lowers the element expression inside
the fill loop, so the IrAlloc re-executes per iteration (runtime heap bump)
and each slot receives its own object, with IR size still O(1) in N.
Covered: flat struct repeat, nested array repeat, struct-in-struct repeat,
three-level repeat, float element repeat. Controls: explicit-list literals
and scalar repeat, which must remain correct.

instruction: Write a Sounio run-pass example named `madaros_assoc_fn_free_callee_body`. A free fn reachable ONLY through an imported module's associated fn must keep its body. spec_dce_scan_item_if_marked used to scan impl methods only when the bare method name was marked, and associated calls. It should compile and run successfully. Expected stdout: AF_ASSOC_FREE_BODY_OK
description: A free fn reachable ONLY through an imported module's associated fn must keep its body. spec_dce_scan_item_if_marked used to scan impl methods only when the bare method name was marked, and associated calls
comments: A free fn reachable ONLY through an imported module's associated fn must
keep its body. spec_dce_scan_item_if_marked used to scan impl methods
only when the bare method name was marked, and associated calls
(AfNum::quad) mark nothing (spec_call_expr_callee_name returns empty for
multi-segment paths) — so af_twice was filtered out of the module's item
list while AfNum::quad still lowered a real call to it. The call bound to
an instr_count==0 stub and the program died on its ud2 (SIGILL rc=132).
Fixed 2026-08-19 by scanning impl/trait method bodies unconditionally:
the filter never deletes an ItemImpl, so a retained body's callees must
be marked. The printed marker is load-bearing — it only prints if
af_twice's body actually ran.

comments: A correlation declared in one function must not reach another.

instruction: Write a Sounio run-pass example named `madaros_hessian_quotient`. hessian_of over the quotient rule. Before this rule existed the division branch cleared the Hessian outright. That was the honest choice at the time -- a missing number rather than an. It should compile and run successfully. Expected stdout: MADAROS_HESSIAN_QUOTIENT_PASS
description: hessian_of over the quotient rule. Before this rule existed the division branch cleared the Hessian outright. That was the honest choice at the time -- a missing number rather than an
comments: hessian_of over the quotient rule.
Before this rule existed the division branch cleared the Hessian outright.
That was the honest choice at the time -- a missing number rather than an
operand's Hessian wearing the quotient's name -- but it meant every ratio
in the clinical corpus (clearance over volume, dose over weight, any
concentration) had a second-order term of exactly zero, and no diagnostic
said so. A confident zero from a shipped builtin is indistinguishable
from a true zero at the call site.
H(a/b)_jk = a_jk/b - (a_j*b_k + a_k*b_j)/b^2 - a*b_jk/b^2 + 2*a*b_j*b_k/b^3
h_bb is the row that pins the rule. A two-term approximation -- the part
that looks like the product rule with a reciprocal -- reproduces h_ab
exactly and gets h_bb wrong, so the mixed partial alone cannot tell a
correct implementation from a plausible one.

instruction: Write a Sounio run-pass example named `madaros_hessian_transcendental`. hessian_of over the transcendental chain rule. Before this rule existed the second-order machinery had storage and a product rule but no chain rule, so hessian_of(x*x) was the correct 2.0. It should compile and run successfully. description: hessian_of over the transcendental chain rule. Before this rule existed the second-order machinery had storage and a product rule but no chain rule, so hessian_of(x*x) was the correct 2.0
comments: hessian_of over the transcendental chain rule.
Before this rule existed the second-order machinery had storage and a
product rule but no chain rule, so hessian_of(x*x) was the correct 2.0
while hessian_of(sin(x)) was a confident 0.0 -- a shipped builtin
returning a plausible wrong answer for every transcendental.
Composite arguments used to be REFUSED because the f'(g)*H(g) term
read s_g² where H_g belonged. The slot held the right register; feeding
it through so_mul_or_none (Lowerer by value) made the multiply see a
leftover s_g². The chain rule is now emitted in place:
H(f(g)) = f''(g)·s_g² + f'(g)·H(g)

description: Regression test: method receiver inference uses declared signature, not heuristics. Bug (pre-fix): infer_method_receiver_use used string-prefix heuristics to decide whether a method call borrows &T, mutably borrows &!T, or moves T.  Methods whose
comments: Regression test: method receiver inference uses declared signature, not heuristics.
Bug (pre-fix): infer_method_receiver_use used string-prefix heuristics to decide
whether a method call borrows &T, mutably borrows &!T, or moves T.  Methods whose
names did not match the heuristic patterns were treated as moves even when the
declared first parameter was &!Self, producing false-positive ownership errors or
silent miscompilation.
Fix: the method call handler now calls scan_fnsig_param_type(FN_SIG[mfi], 0) to
read the actual declared receiver type.  If SCAN_TY==10 and ref_hash_mut!=0 the
receiver is an exclusive borrow (&!Self): borrow conflict checks are enforced and
the borrow is released after the call.  No heuristic string matching is used.
This test verifies:
1. A struct method declared with &!Self can mutate state without a false positive.
2. The ownership checker permits a second &!Self call on the same variable after
the first call's ephemeral borrow has been released.
3. A &Self (shared) method may be called while no exclusive borrow is active.
4. main() returns 0 (success) when all mutations produce the expected values.

description: Golden regression test that DISTINGUISHES a correct SRET-by-value compile from a move-codegen aliasing miscompile of the hazard `c = combine(c, g(c))`. V4 is a SMALL aggregate (4 i64) so today's copy-everywhere souc compiles and
comments: Golden regression test that DISTINGUISHES a correct SRET-by-value compile

V4 is a SMALL aggregate (4 i64) so today's copy-everywhere souc compiles and

Two hazard variants, to cover both inner-slot aliasing and arg-order
sensitivity (the future arg-move wedge):
Leg 1:  c = combine(c, g(c))     (inner SRET g(c) may clobber c's slot)
Leg 2:  d = combine(g(d), d)     (arg order swapped; 2nd arg d may be
clobbered by g(d)'s SRET into d's slot)
Values chosen with a place-weighted checksum so correct and broken numbers
diverge and cannot collide:
CORRECT  combine reads ORIGINAL start in both legs -> {11, 22, 33, 44}
BROKEN   start clobbered to g(start) first -> combine({10,20,30,40},
checksum(v) = v.a*1 + v.b*10 + v.c*100 + v.d*1000
packed = checksum(c) * 1000000 + checksum(d)
any break in either leg -> a DIFFERENT packed integer

comments: N2 negative control (codex ruling 2026-08-23, round 3 -- grok-4.6's
env-φ finding): `var x = measure(1); if c { x = measure(2) }; use(x)`
must NOT let x's post-if type revert to measure(1)'s narrow set. The bug
was structural, not just "wrong branch wins": checker_check_block_inplace
push_scope()s/pop_scope()s around every block including if-arms, and
pop_scope discards ANY env rebind made inside -- so the reassignment
literally never reached anywhere outside the branch, AS IF it had not
happened. checker_merge_ns_reassigned_inplace (called at the if/match
merge point) closes this: reassigning a Knowledge var while
ns_branch_depth > 0 records the name instead of a rebind that would just
be discarded, and the merge re-binds it in the NOW-RESTORED outer scope
with noise_set_id forced to top.
The observable proof is NOT just the "env_join" trace line at the merge
(that only proves the merge RAN) -- it's reading x again afterward: `x +
w3` unions x's POST-merge type with an empty set, so its own "union=-1"
line is the end-to-end proof that the forced-top value actually survived
past the if-statement into the code that follows it.
Per-rule sabotage: SOUNIO_NS_SABOTAGE_JOIN=1 disables the env-merge
(same knob as the CFG-join fixes), reproducing the pre-fix bug: x reverts

correct N2 behaviour, not a bug: call typing comes from the callee's

call result, a second "NS_TRACE measure=<h2>" line for the fresh measured
value, and a final "NS_TRACE union=-1" line -- unknown absorbs the real
singleton rather than the union silently reverting to just h2.

description: -O must not propagate values across basic-block boundaries (#1667)
comments: Four ocp_mfi_* peels -- dedup_imm, const_fold, copy_prop and sccp -- were
linear scans carrying a propagation table from the first instruction of a
function to the last, with no invalidation at labels or terminators. A value
established in one arm of an if/else reached the other arm and the join.
Measured symptom before the fix, with s printed after each if/else:

Each of the four caused it INDEPENDENTLY, which is why disabling them one at a
time found nothing; all four had to be disabled at once for the program to
come out right.
The same defect made a loop containing a loop-invariant constant and a call
HANG under -O, which is the second part below.

passes do not run at all and it passes vacuously.

instruction: Write a Sounio run-pass example named `opt_compact_nops_preserves_names`. #1649: ocp_mfi_compact_nops moves every surviving instruction down to close the gaps left by removed nops, and ocp_mfi_instr_move_fields moved each lane by hand. The name lane was moved with. It should compile and run successfully. Expected stdout: alpha=1 beta=2
description: #1649: ocp_mfi_compact_nops moves every surviving instruction down to close the gaps left by removed nops, and ocp_mfi_instr_move_fields moved each lane by hand. The name lane was moved with
comments: #1649: ocp_mfi_compact_nops moves every surviving instruction down to close
the gaps left by removed nops, and ocp_mfi_instr_move_fields moved each lane
by hand. The name lane was moved with
ir_arena_name(<dst slot>) = nm
and ir_arena_name is a GETTER returning a Name by value, so the assignment
wrote nothing: the destination slot kept the previous occupant's name. String
constants therefore printed some OTHER instruction's name after any -O run
that removed a nop -- literally `print_char` in place of the literal, or
nothing at all.
A transform artifact of the SoA conversion: the original
`X.instrs[d].name = X.instrs[s].name` had its left-hand side rewritten into
the getter. Notably the compiler ACCEPTS assignment to a call result, so
nothing flagged it.
Deliberately uses no multi-argument call: those miscompile under -O for an
unrelated reason (#1667), and this test must fail for its own reason only.
The if/else is what leaves a nop for compaction to remove.
Before the fix this printed "12" -- values right, both labels gone entirely.

An f64 returned from a call came back as garbage under -O: half(5.0)  ->  9223372036854775808.000000    instead of 2.5 ocp_mfi_compact_nops removed every IrNop, and the lowering emits a NOP. description: An f64 returned from a call came back as garbage under -O: half(5.0)  ->  9223372036854775808.000000    instead of 2.5 ocp_mfi_compact_nops removed every IrNop, and the lowering emits a NOP
comments: An f64 returned from a call came back as garbage under -O:
ocp_mfi_compact_nops removed every IrNop, and the lowering emits a NOP
carrying IR_FLOAT_REG_MARKER_FLAG (64064) to tell codegen that a register
holds f64 -- codegen_x86_linux.sio:7406 says so outright, "Always honor an
explicit float-marker IrNop". With the marker gone the register is read as an
integer, so the bit pattern comes back as i64 MAX.
Five lines, and it reproduced on origin/main as well as on the #1649 branch,
so it was never about the arena. It is also why an epistemic variance read
back as 0.000000 under -O -- the shadow value is an f64 reached through this
same marker -- and why tests/run-pass/knowledge_octonion_structure.sio lost
its variance under -O while passing without it.
Only meaningful run BOTH with and without -O: without it the peel never runs.
Refs #1649

//@ run-pass
// tests/run-pass/pediatric_pbpk_receipt.sio
// Full paediatric PBPK receipt (v6). Avoids examples/** claim conflicts.

use clinical::pediatric_pbpk::{
    ped_selftest, ped_selftest_v6,
    ped_child_5yr, ped_neonate_term_2wk, ped_preterm_ga28_2wk,
    ped_vanco_noisy_tdm_child_default, ped_vanco_accumulation,
}

fn main() -> i32 with IO, Mut, Div, Panic {
    print("PED_RECEIPT_BEGIN\n")
    let n0 = ped_selftest()
    print("PED_RECEIPT_BASE ")
    print_int(n0)
    print("\n")
    let n1 = ped_selftest_v6()
    print("PED_RECEIPT_V6 ")
    print_int(n1)
    print("\n")
    let n = n0 + n1
    print("PED_RECEIPT_ALL ")
    print_int(n)
    print("\n")

    let child = ped_child_5yr()
    let tdm = ped_vanco_noisy_tdm_child_default(&child)
    print("PED_TDM fixed%=")
    print_f64(tdm.pct_fixed)
    print(" noisy%=")
    print_f64(tdm.pct_noisy)
    print(" perfect%=")
    print_f64(tdm.pct_perfect)
    print("\n")
    print("PED_TDM noisy_auc p05=")
    print_f64(tdm.auc_noisy_p05)
    print(" mean=")
    print_f64(tdm.auc_noisy_mean)
    print(" p95=")
    print_f64(tdm.auc_noisy_p95)
    print("\n")

    let neo = ped_neonate_term_2wk()
    let pre = ped_preterm_ga28_2wk()
    let an = ped_vanco_accumulation(&neo, 15.0 * neo.weight_kg, 12.0, 6)
    let ap = ped_vanco_accumulation(&pre, 15.0 * pre.weight_kg, 12.0, 6)
    print("PED_ACC_NEO r=")
    print_f64(an.r)
    print(" frac1=")
    print_f64(an.frac_cmin_dose1)
    print(" d90=")
    print_int(an.doses_to_90pct_cmin)
    print("\n")
    print("PED_ACC_PRETERM r=")
    print_f64(ap.r)
    print(" frac1=")
    print_f64(ap.frac_cmin_dose1)
    print(" d90=")
    print_int(ap.doses_to_90pct_cmin)
    print("\n")

    if n0 == 16 && n1 == 2 && n == 18
        && tdm.pct_fixed < tdm.pct_noisy
        && tdm.pct_noisy < tdm.pct_perfect {
        print("PEDIATRIC_PBPK_OK\n")
        print("PEDIATRIC_PBPK_V6_OK\n")
        0
    } else {
        print("PEDIATRIC_PBPK_FAILED\n")
        1
    }
}

instruction: Write a Sounio run-pass example named `println_zero_arg_newline`. Zero-arg `println()` must emit a newline and nothing else. ir/lower.sio lowered `println(x)` to `print_kind(x); print_char('\n')` and emitted the payload call UNCONDITIONALLY. description: Zero-arg `println()` must emit a newline and nothing else. ir/lower.sio lowered `println(x)` to `print_kind(x); print_char('\n')` and emitted the payload call UNCONDITIONALLY. With no arguments the callee's
comments: Zero-arg `println()` must emit a newline and nothing else.
ir/lower.sio lowered `println(x)` to `print_kind(x); print_char('\n')` and
emitted the payload call UNCONDITIONALLY. With no arguments the callee's
char* parameter register is never written, so `print` walked whatever
address was last in rdi looking for a NUL. Measured on a from-source
Madaros before the guard, this file's first `println()` SIGSEGVs (rc=139)
after printing `A` -- the process never reaches the sentinel below.
This is not a hypothetical form: measured 2026-08-28, the tree holds 321
zero-arg `println()` call sites across 19 files, 23 of them in
examples/uncertainty.sio alone.
The test is self-checking by ARRIVAL. It cannot assert the ABSENCE of a
spurious payload from inside the process, so the markers are placed so a
payload would be visible in stdout to a reader: correct output is exactly

"A
B

PRINTLN_ZERO_ARG_OK
", and the byte-exact form is pinned outside
the harness (the //@ expect-stdout directive above is a contains-check).

description: L0 acceptance for product_nonassoc (stdlib/epistemic/product_nonassoc.sio) — the wiring that turns non-associativity into epistemic variance automatically. A scalar observable with base GUM variance 0.25,
comments: L0 acceptance for product_nonassoc (stdlib/epistemic/product_nonassoc.sio) —
the wiring that turns non-associativity into epistemic variance automatically.
A scalar observable with base GUM variance 0.25,
computed through an octonion triple:
Fano  (e1,e2,e3): associator = 0   ⇒ variance unchanged       (0.25)
non-Fano (e1,e2,e4): ‖α‖² = 4, κ=1 ⇒ variance += κ·4 = total   (4.25)
This is the join of the two theses: non-associativity does not merely get
blocked at the optimizer — it FEEDS the uncertainty budget through the
propagation engine, with certainty-of-order something you earn (Fano triple),
not assume.
Madaros-native path (2026-07-20): field-form Epistemic + leaf module
(PnOct self-contained associator). No algebra::octonion import. Historic
import was epistemic::propagate::product_nonassoc.

instruction: Write a Sounio run-pass example named `rapamycin_epistemic_adaptive`. β⁵ inter-procedural variance propagation enabled: mutable f64 vars use fixed runtime variance slots so variance_of() tracks across loop iterations and function call boundaries. EPISTEMIC ADAPTIVE ODE — FIRST IMPLEMENTATION. It should compile and run successfully. Expected stdout: PASS
description: β⁵ inter-procedural variance propagation enabled: mutable f64 vars use fixed runtime variance slots so variance_of() tracks across loop iterations and function call boundaries. EPISTEMIC ADAPTIVE ODE — FIRST IMPLEMENTATION
comments: β⁵ inter-procedural variance propagation enabled: mutable f64 vars use fixed runtime
variance slots so variance_of() tracks across loop iterations and function call boundaries.
EPISTEMIC ADAPTIVE ODE — FIRST IMPLEMENTATION
Bogacki-Shampine 3(2) with variance-aware lookbehind step control
NOVELTY: first ODE integrator that combines numerical error control with
metrological variance-growth control, using a lookbehind (post-step,
next-step) adaptive strategy:
After each in-place step:
err_norm    = |e_num| / (atol + rtol·|y|)         [numerical]
v_growth    = variance_of(y) − var_pre             [metrological]
u_ratio     = v_growth / (u_atol + u_rtol·var_pre)
dt_num   = dt · safety · (1/err_norm)^(1/3)       [3rd-order method]
dt_epist = dt · safety · (1/u_ratio)^(1/2)         [variance ~ dt²]
dt_next  = min(dt_num, dt_epist)
Why lookbehind rather than trial-and-reject:
The Sounio compiler's GUM variance propagation is reliable for in-place
mutation (var = var + …) but has limited depth for trial-then-commit
patterns in deep expression chains. Lookbehind control achieves the same
adaptive effect without rollback — the next step's dt is informed by the
current step's observed variance growth.
Method: Bogacki-Shampine 3(2) (default in MATLAB ode23)
Model:  Rapamycin 3-compartment PBPK (blood, brain, peripheral)
Ref:    JCGM 100:2008 (GUM), Bogacki & Shampine (1989)

description: Rapamycin (Sirolimus) Epistemic PBPK Test Suite Validates GUM-based uncertainty propagation through a 3-compartment rapamycin model: Blood, Brain (BBB-limited), Peripheral (fast-eq. tissues).
comments: Rapamycin (Sirolimus) Epistemic PBPK Test Suite
Validates GUM-based uncertainty propagation through a 3-compartment
rapamycin model: Blood, Brain (BBB-limited), Peripheral (fast-eq. tissues).
Model choice: Distribution-capped 3-compartment (NOT full 14-compartment).
- Brain compartment: kp_brain=0.08 (P-gp efflux at BBB) — PRESERVED accurately
- Peripheral: v_periph=50L, kp_periph=0.5 → t1/2 ~ 21h (tractable for 48h)
- Adipose deep sequestration (kp_adipose~15) excluded by design
(would require multi-week simulation for CL to be observable in AUC)
Epistemic parameters:
- cl_hepatic: 12.4 L/h, Var=54.76 (CV=60%, CYP3A4 polymorphism, Ferron 1997)
- kp_brain: 0.08, Var=0.000625 (SD=0.025, P-gp efflux, Lampen 1998)
- fu_plasma: 0.08, Var=0.0004 (SD=0.02, 92% bound, Schreiber 1991)
GUM step sizes: h = max(1e-6 * |mean|, 1e-2 * SD)  [GPT review correction]
Confidence: evidence-quality score [0,1], NOT Beta distribution
(Beta appropriate only for [0,1]-bounded quantities; CL is unbounded)
6 tests:
1. Simulation completes successfully
2. Brain/plasma ratio < 0.15 (P-gp efflux verified)
3. CV(AUC_0_48) > 30% (CYP3A4 inter-individual variability)
4. All epistemic variances > 0
5. AUC(CL/2) > AUC(CL_ref) — causal monotonicity check
6. CL dominates AUC uncertainty: s_cl > 0.5

description: GUM-vs-Monte-Carlo validation for rapamycin 3-compartment PBPK Validates that GUM linearized uncertainty propagation (finite-difference Jacobian) agrees with Monte Carlo sampling to within an order of magnitude.
comments: GUM-vs-Monte-Carlo validation for rapamycin 3-compartment PBPK
Validates that GUM linearized uncertainty propagation (finite-difference
Jacobian) agrees with Monte Carlo sampling to within an order of magnitude.

MC path: N=200 samples, each parameter drawn as mean + sigma * z
where z ~ Normal(0,1) via CLT (sum of 12 uniform - 6).
Sample variance of c_blood computed from MC ensemble.
Acceptance criterion: ratio of GUM variance to MC variance between
0.1 and 10.0 (same order of magnitude). GUM is linearized, MC
captures nonlinearity, so exact match is not expected.
Model: 3-compartment rapamycin (blood, brain, peripheral)

instruction: Write a Sounio run-pass example named `rapamycin_iso_budget`. RAPAMYCIN 3-COMPARTMENT PBPK — ISO UNCERTAINTY BUDGET (JCGM 100:2008 §8) Three uncertain pharmacokinetic parameters, each assigned a budget channel: ch0: CL_hepatic = 12.4 ± 1.24 L/h  (10% CV — TDM assay precision). It should compile and run successfully. Expected stdout: PASS
description: RAPAMYCIN 3-COMPARTMENT PBPK — ISO UNCERTAINTY BUDGET (JCGM 100:2008 §8) Three uncertain pharmacokinetic parameters, each assigned a budget channel: ch0: CL_hepatic = 12.4 ± 1.24 L/h  (10% CV — TDM assay precision)
comments: RAPAMYCIN 3-COMPARTMENT PBPK — ISO UNCERTAINTY BUDGET (JCGM 100:2008 §8)
Three uncertain pharmacokinetic parameters, each assigned a budget channel:
ch0: CL_hepatic = 12.4 ± 1.24 L/h  (10% CV — TDM assay precision)
ch1: Kp_brain   = 0.08 ± 0.008      (10% CV — in vitro partition assay)
ch2: fu_plasma  = 0.08 ± 0.008      (10% CV — ultrafiltration assay)
GUM linearization requires sigma << |x|; 10% CV is the practical limit.
One model run produces the full per-parameter variance decomposition.
SOTA: No existing PK/PD tool (NONMEM, Monolix, Phoenix) can do this.
Dose: 6 mg IV rapamycin (Cypher stent loading dose)
Integration: 20 Euler steps, h = 0.1 h, t_final = 2 h
Note: GUM linearization diverges beyond ~5h for this model due to the
c_brain/Kp_brain division (b^4 amplification with small Kp). This is a
genuine limitation that motivates the GUM-vs-MC comparison in the dissertation.
This test exercises TWO independent variance paths:
(a) Knowledge<f64> propagation through Sounio's Epistemic effect
— variance_of(c_blood) reflects accumulated GUM-through-arithmetic.
(b) Explicit per-parameter Budget64 via finite-difference Jacobian
— gives ISO §8 ranked attribution that (a) cannot expose per channel.
Cross-check: the two paths must agree within finite-diff tolerance.

instruction: Write a Sounio run-pass example named `reinhart_rogoff`. Reinhart-Rogoff 2010 Reproducibility Demo The 2010 R-R paper "Growth in a Time of Debt" claimed countries with debt/GDP > 90% suffer mean growth of -0.1%, driving a decade of austerity. It should compile and run successfully.
description: Reinhart-Rogoff 2010 Reproducibility Demo The 2010 R-R paper "Growth in a Time of Debt" claimed countries with debt/GDP > 90% suffer mean growth of -0.1%, driving a decade of austerity
comments: Reinhart-Rogoff 2010 Reproducibility Demo
The 2010 R-R paper "Growth in a Time of Debt" claimed countries with
debt/GDP > 90% suffer mean growth of -0.1%, driving a decade of austerity
in the EU, US, and UK.
Herndon, Ash, Pollin (2013) found three compounding errors:
1. UNIT ERROR:    growth stored as percentage points but treated as fractions
2. SAMPLE ERROR:  Excel formula excluded 5 high-debt, high-growth countries
3. UNCERTAINTY:   4 country-observations — result was within noise floor
Corrected result: +2.2% growth (not -0.1%). The threshold claim was noise.
This demo shows all three errors in Sounio's epistemic tracking:
- Units: explicit fraction/pp conversion — confusion is visible
- Provenance: excluded sample is a missing branch in the computation graph
- Uncertainty: SNR < 1 makes the "threshold effect" formally indefensible
Data sources: Herndon, Ash, Pollin (2013) Table 3; HAP Working Paper 322.

instruction: Write a Sounio run-pass example named `return_nested_array_literal`. IGNORED because it does not pass yet, and the reason is worth keeping in the tree rather than in a note. Returning a nested array literal from a function declared to return a 2-D. It should compile and run successfully. Expected stdout: nested array return: PASS
description: IGNORED because it does not pass yet, and the reason is worth keeping in the tree rather than in a note. Returning a nested array literal from a function declared to return a 2-D
comments: IGNORED because it does not pass yet, and the reason is worth keeping in the
tree rather than in a note.
Returning a nested array literal from a function declared to return a 2-D
array is rejected: `error: return type does not match function signature`.
The flat case is accepted, so the gap is specific to the nested encoding. The
declared type comes from scan_type and the literal builds its own hash from
its first element, and the two do not agree. Element size is NOT the
discriminator -- [[f64; 1]; 2], whose inner element is 8 bytes, is rejected
too, so a first guess that scan_type computes a real element size while the
literal hardcodes 8 is disproven.
This matters beyond arrays. The return-type check currently reports through
tc_error, which prints "warning: " and does not fail the build (see the note
at its definition). Pointing it at tc_error_hard makes it fatal and works --
it correctly rejects hello.sio and bdf_stiff.sio, which really are ill-typed
-- but it also rejects this, and stdlib/numerical/linalg.sio mat7_to_nested,
which are correct. So the return position cannot be made to fail a build
until this is fixed, and that is the whole dependency: nothing else in the
study's 24 modules or in 1893 run-pass tests is affected.
When this passes, drop the ignore, and the return check can become fatal.

instruction: Write a Sounio run-pass example named `rng_fused_global_read_single_eval`. effectful call fused with an array read in one let evaluates ONCE (#1569). It should compile and run successfully.
description: effectful call fused with an array read in one let evaluates ONCE (#1569)
comments: #1569: the legacy scalar-variance algebra in lower_expr_variance_ref
re-lowered operand VALUES to feed emit_variance_independent_product/div.
When the operand held an effectful call, the call ran TWICE per
evaluation, so `let d = W[k] * (rng_next() % 10000)` advanced the PRNG
twice per iteration on Madaros and the stream diverged from lean_single.
The fix skips the value re-lowering whenever an operand subtree may
contain a call (variance of a call result is untracked anyway).
Witness: the same computation runs fused (the #1569 shape) and hoisted
(call in its own let); the two sequences must match element for element.
Integer arithmetic only, so the pin is exact on every engine. The global
array is zero-initialised and runtime-assigned on purpose — a separate,
pre-existing lean_single defect reads literal-initialised GLOBAL arrays
as element 0 in fused expressions (out of scope here; see the #1569
discussion), so a literal initialiser would pin the WRONG value on lean.

IS a genuine group: the sedenion SIGNED-AUTOMORPHISM group. A linear map M in GL(4,2) (acting on
indices 1..15 as F_2^4 vectors, preserving xor) is a signed automorphism iff the sign ratio
sigma(Mi,Mj)*sigma(i,j) is a COBOUNDARY delta(eps)(i,j) = eps(i)eps(j)eps(i^j) for some signs eps.
This test counts them exactly:
* octonions {1..7}: ALL 168 = |GL(3,2)| linear maps are signed automorphisms;
* sedenions {1..15}: exactly 168 of the |GL(4,2)| = 20160 linear maps are  (= the SAME 168);
* every sedenion automorphism FIXES e8 (index 8) — the doubling seam is the unique fixed point.
So 168 is the group Aut ~ PSL(2,7); 1848 = 11*168 is NOT a group order (the 11 is combinatorial).

comments: FRONTIER (Paper 1 open item) — the exact Cayley-Dickson product over UNBOUNDED ℚ, ALL 16 components.
The i64 version (sedenion_cd_full16_q.sio) does the full 16-comp ℚ product via the common-denominator
reduction, but caps at coefficients ~1e8 (i64 output). This closes the unbounded case with a minimal,
self-contained SIGNED BigInt (base 1e9 limbs) — so numerators/denominators are ARBITRARY precision.
WHY A LOCAL BigInt. The stdlib `math::bignat` full big×big `big_mul` SIGSEGVs under souc v0.80.0
(a single `big_mul(a,b)`, no arrays, no loop — a clean #651/#637 struct-copy repro), and `[BigInt;16]`
SIGSEGVs (the array-of-structs wall). This brick CIRCUMVENTS both — it does NOT fix #651 — exactly as
the i64 common-denom circumvented #637: (i) a minimal in-file BigInt built only from primitives that
empirically compile (schoolbook big×big = big_mul_small + limb-shift + big_add-in-loop, which the spike
confirms runs); (ii) the 16 numerators are held in FLAT scalar arrays [i64;N], never [BigInt;16].
Common-denom identity: a rational sedenion = 16 integer numerators A[16] over a common denom Ad;
(A·B)[k] = (Σ_{i⊕j=k} σ(i,j) A[i] B[j]) / (Ad·Bd)  — an INTEGER 16-comp product of numerators.
Certified on two cases: (1) a known zero divisor scaled by 10^40 — product EXACTLY 0 in all 16 comps
at magnitude 10^80 (i64 would overflow into garbage; exactness holds); (2) a general 16-comp product
with unbounded rational coefficients (components up to ~10^70). Each component's residue mod 1e9+7 is
emitted (byte-identical across souc builds; a per-limb decimal printer is miscompiled differently by
bin/souc vs stage2) and cross-verified vs the Python oracle; the EXACT decimals are witnessed by Lean
(native Int, SounioCDqbig.lean) and the oracle (exact ℚ). Case 1's annihilation is checked structurally.

comments: FRENTE B, vector 4/3 (physics) — the sedenion left-multiplication algebra is Cℓ(8), executed.
Deep-research (peer-reviewed: Gresnigt et al., EPJC 2019 s10052-019-6967-1 / 2024 s10052-024-13476-0;
arXiv 2306.13098) establishes: the left-multiplication algebra of the complexified sedenions ℂ⊗𝕊 is
the Clifford algebra Cℓ(8) ≅ ℂ(16) (256 = 2^8 maps), the rank-4 step up from the octonionic Cℓ(6)
(64 = 2^6) that underlies Furey's one-generation SM construction. This test certifies the Clifford
PRESENTATION exactly: the eight left-multiplication operators L_1..L_8 pairwise anticommute and each
squares to −I — eight anticommuting √(−I) generators = a Cℓ(8) presentation. The 8th generator is
L_8 = e_8, the octonion→sedenion doubling unit (so e_8 is exactly the extra Clifford generator).
Uses the SPARSE identity: e_i·e_k = σ(i,k)·e_{i⊕k}, so L_i has one entry σ(i,k) per column k at row
i⊕k. Then (L_i L_j)[r][c] = σ(i,j⊕c)σ(j,c) at row r=i⊕j⊕c, giving:
{L_i,L_j}[i⊕j⊕c][c] = σ(i,j⊕c)σ(j,c) + σ(j,i⊕c)σ(i,c)   (anticommute ⟺ 0 ∀c)
(L_i²)[c][c] = σ(i,i⊕c)σ(i,c)                             (= −I ⟺ all −1)
No matrix multiplication needed. Also verified: 42 of the 105 pairs {L_i,L_j} do NOT anticommute
(the sedenion non-associativity signature), and ALL 42 are lower-upper (touch the doubling half);
the maximal mutually-anticommuting set has 8 generators ⟹ ladder rank 4; and the Gresnigt
S3-invariant charge Q_1 = (N_1+N_2+N_3 − 3 N_4)/3 on the 2^4 Fock space gives the SM electric-charge
multiset {0, ±1/3, ±2/3, ±1}. (The physical THREE-GENERATION interpretation of Cℓ(8)/S3 is a

comments: FRENTE B, vector 4/3 — cross-check of Gresnigt's three generation-octonions + an explicit G₂
(COLOR-side) monomial automorphism permuting them. Executed against the primary source.
Gresnigt (EPJC 2019/2024; arXiv:2306.13098) builds three fermion generations from three octonion
subalgebras of the sedenions 𝕊 sharing a common quaternion, cyclically related by the family S₃.
The paper's three copies (its basis, App. A) are, as index sets:
sharing the quaternion ℍ = ⟨e₄,e₈,e₁₂⟩ = {4,8,12}.
This test certifies, in this repo's Cayley-Dickson convention:
(a) each 𝕆_i is a genuine (zero-divisor-free) octonion, all three ambient-equivalent (each has 6
non-anticommuting internal left-mult pairs in the 16-dim Cℓ(8));  ℍ = 𝕆₁∩𝕆₂∩𝕆₃ = {4,8,12};
(b) the pure 3-cycle φ = (e₁e₂e₃)(e₅e₆e₇)(e₉e₁₀e₁₁)(e₁₃e₁₄e₁₅) [all signs +1, fixing e₀,e₄,e₈,e₁₂]
is a genuine algebra automorphism of 𝕊 (all 256 products), of order 3, cyclically permuting
𝕆₁→𝕆₂→𝕆₃ and fixing ℍ and e₈;
(c) φ = g ⊕ g is DIAGONAL under 𝕊 = 𝕆 ⊕ 𝕆·e₈ with g = (e₁e₂e₃)(e₅e₆e₇) an automorphism of the base
octonion {e₁..e₇} — so φ ∈ G₂ = Aut(𝕆).
HONEST BOUNDARY (this is NOT a physics bridge). Because φ ∈ G₂ and G₂ ⊃ SU(3)_color, φ is a
COLOR-sector operation. It is NOT Gresnigt's family S₃: by Brown's theorem Aut(𝕊)=G₂×S₃, and the
family S₃ is precisely the direct factor DISJOINT from G₂ (non-monomial) — used exactly so that
family ≠ color. This brick therefore does NOT connect the zero-divisor monomial-168 to fermion
generations, and does NOT amend Erratum E1 (which correctly places the monomial-168 inside G₂). It
reproduces the paper's octonion triple and exhibits the G₂/color realization of their 3-set
permutation — nothing more. A genuine bridge would require building the fermion ideals and showing
Brown's S₃ acts on those states as a monomial-168 element; that is not done here.
Decidable integer arithmetic, no float. SELF-CONTAINED. Cross-verified vs the oracle by the gate + Lean.

* NSUB = 15 subspaces total;
* ZDFREE = 8 are zero-divisor-free (genuine octonion / division algebra); the other 7 contain a
zero divisor — the quasi-octonions (matches Cawagas, Discuss. Math. 2004: 7 quasi-octonions carry
the sedenion zero divisors);

({L_i,L_j}=0 in the 16-dim Cℓ(8), see sedenion_clifford8.md): the base octonion {e_1..e_7}.

ambient-L non-anticommuting-pair counts {0, 6, 12}.

prove — Erratum E1's claim that Gresnigt's three family-S₃ octonion copies are non-monomial: only the

inside the monomial-168. Reported as an executed algebraic fingerprint, not a group-theoretic proof.

description: FRENTE B — the e₈-seam bridge: zero-division (state level) and operator non-alternativity are ONE locus. This closes the previously disconnected state-level (§1 e₈-boundary, Paper 1/2) and operator-level (Cℓ(6)→Cℓ(8) fingerprint, this vector) strata of 𝕊. For a lower×upper index-pair (l,u) with l∈{1..7},
comments: FRENTE B — the e₈-seam bridge: zero-division (state level) and operator non-alternativity are ONE locus.
This closes the previously disconnected state-level (§1 e₈-boundary, Paper 1/2) and operator-level
(Cℓ(6)→Cℓ(8) fingerprint, this vector) strata of 𝕊. For a lower×upper index-pair (l,u) with l∈{1..7},
u∈{8..15}, the following are equivalent (proved analytically for the forward direction; certified for
all 56 pairs):
• {L_l, L_u} ≠ 0          (the left-multiplications fail to anticommute);
• (L_l L_u)² ≠ −I;
• e_l + e_u is a left zero divisor of 𝕊;
• (l,u) is OFF the e₈ seam  (seam = {u=8 or l⊕u=8}).
The anticommutator is the exact OBSTRUCTION to zero-division: if {L_l,L_u}=0 then, using L_l²=L_u²=−I,
(L_l L_u)² = L_l(L_u L_l)L_u = −L_l² L_u² = −(−I)(−I) = −I,
so spec(L_l L_u) ⊆ {±i}; +1 is excluded, L_l+L_u is nonsingular, and e_l+e_u is NOT a zero divisor.
(The determinant/eigenvalue formulations of the theorem and the 4-regular quartet incidence are in the
oracle; here we certify the sparse-checkable equivalences over ℤ.)
Sparse identities (no matrix products): with e_i e_j = σ(i,j) e_{i⊕j},
{L_l,L_u}=0        ⟺  σ(l,u⊕c)σ(u,c) + σ(u,l⊕c)σ(l,c) = 0        ∀c
(L_l L_u)²=−I      ⟺  σ(l,l⊕c)σ(u,l⊕u⊕c)σ(l,u⊕c)σ(u,c) = −1      ∀c
e_l+e_u is a ZD    ⟺  ∃ primitive e_a±e_b annihilated by (e_l+e_u)
Then: {L_l,L_u}=0  ⟺  (L_lL_u)²=−I  ⟺  NOT ZD  ⟺  on the e₈ seam, for all 56 pairs; and the three
42-element sets (non-anticommuting pairs, ZD-participating directions, off-seam pairs) coincide.
Decidable integer arithmetic, no float. SELF-CONTAINED. Cross-verified vs the oracle + Lean.

comments: FRENTE B, vector 4(1) — the emergent metric: the ZD geometry's graphs have INTEGRAL spectra.
The zero-divisor geometry is not just combinatorial — its graphs carry an exact spectral (metric)
structure. Both are spectrally integral:
* a fiber (K_{6,6} - 3*K_{2,2}, 12 vertices, degree 4): adjacency spectrum {4, 2^2, 0^6, -2^2, -4},
Laplacian {0, 2^2, 4^6, 6^2, 8}, algebraic connectivity (spectral gap) = 2;
* the 2*K_7 fiber-incidence graph (7 fibers, each pair doubled, degree 12): adjacency {12, -2^6},
Laplacian {0, 14^6}, algebraic connectivity = 14.
We certify the integral spectra by their SPECTRAL MOMENTS: trace(A^k) = sum of k-th powers of the
eigenvalues, computed exactly over Z by integer matrix powers. Matching the moments of a proposed
integral spectrum (for k up to > #distinct eigenvalues) pins the spectrum.
Decidable integer arithmetic, no float. SELF-CONTAINED. Cross-verified vs
scripts/research/sedenion_spectra_oracle.py by the gate + Lean.

Brick 2 (sedenion_zd_fibers.sio) proved the 84 participating primitives split into 7 fibers of
12 vertices / 24 edges / degree 4. This proves WHAT each fiber IS: every fiber is isomorphic to
K_{6,6}  minus a 2-factor of three disjoint 4-cycles  (= K_{6,6} - 3*K_{2,2}),

the COMMON-NEIGHBOR PROFILE. Over the 66 vertex-pairs of a fiber, the number of common annihilators

* 4  for 6  pairs   (co-blocked: same side, same K_{2,2} block),
* 2  for 24 pairs   (same side, different block),
* 0  for 36 pairs   (opposite sides — bipartite, so no common neighbor).

6+6 (brick 2). (The rigorous "complement = three 4-cycles" isomorphism is confirmed by the Python
oracle + Lean, which can traverse the graph; this test executes the profile, which needs none.)

lo^hi != 8, and among participants lo^hi in {9..15} is precisely the fiber label. (The companion
facts "each fiber is connected + bipartite 6+6" are verified in the Python oracle; this test

description: variance_of() implemented via β⁴ shadow buffer in lean_single.sio Sedenion zero-divisor confidence-collapse demonstration. Classical Moreno (1998) / Smith (1995) result: the sedenion algebra S
comments: variance_of() implemented via β⁴ shadow buffer in lean_single.sio
Sedenion zero-divisor confidence-collapse demonstration.
Classical Moreno (1998) / Smith (1995) result: the sedenion algebra S
(dimension 16, the Cayley-Dickson double of the octonions) loses
alternativity and contains ZERO DIVISORS — non-zero a, b in S with
a*b = 0. The stdlib uses the canonical example
satisfying a*b = 0 under the standard Cayley-Dickson sign convention
(verified against stdlib math::sedenion).
CONFIDENCE-COLLAPSE EVENT
When the four scalar coefficients (alpha, beta, gamma, delta) carrying
the zero-divisor pair are themselves uncertain, the algebraic identity
a*b = 0 produces an output whose mean is exactly zero but whose GUM
variance is strictly positive. The signal-to-noise ratio formally
collapses: |E[a*b]| = 0, var(a*b) > 0.
This is the epistemic singularity Sounio is uniquely positioned to
detect at the type/effect level. A first-order GUM analysis around the
zero-divisor locus is performed below by hand-deriving two output
components of the sedenion product and tracking variance through the
scalar arithmetic shadow buffer.

// Build a main that loads f64 1.5 into rdi and calls print_f64, then exit(0)
fn emit_main(code: CodeBuffer, print_f64_off: i64) -> CodeBuffer with Mut {
    var c = code
    // mov rax, IEEE754(1.5) = 0x3FF8000000000000
    c = emit_byte(c, 0x48); c = emit_byte(c, 0xb8)
    c = emit_byte(c, 0x00); c = emit_byte(c, 0x00); c = emit_byte(c, 0x00); c = emit_byte(c, 0x00)
    c = emit_byte(c, 0x00); c = emit_byte(c, 0x00); c = emit_byte(c, 0xf8); c = emit_byte(c, 0x3f)
    // mov rdi, rax
    c = emit_byte(c, 0x48); c = emit_byte(c, 0x89); c = emit_byte(c, 0xc7)
    // call print_f64 (rel32)
    let call_site = c.len
    c = emit_byte(c, 0xe8)
    let rel = print_f64_off - (call_site + 5)
    c = emit_byte(c, rel & 0xFF)
    c = emit_byte(c, (rel >> 8) & 0xFF)
    c = emit_byte(c, (rel >> 16) & 0xFF)
    c = emit_byte(c, (rel >> 24) & 0xFF)
    // mov edi, 0 (exit code)
    c = emit_byte(c, 0xbf); c = emit_byte(c, 0x00); c = emit_byte(c, 0x00); c = emit_byte(c, 0x00); c = emit_byte(c, 0x00)
    // mov eax, 60 (sys_exit)
    c = emit_byte(c, 0xb8); c = emit_byte(c, 0x3c); c = emit_byte(c, 0x00); c = emit_byte(c, 0x00); c = emit_byte(c, 0x00)
    // syscall
    c = emit_byte(c, 0x0f); c = emit_byte(c, 0x05)
    c
}

fn emit_u16(buf: [i8; 4096], off: i64, v: i64) -> [i8; 4096] with Mut {
    var b = buf
    b[(off) as usize] = (v & 0xFF) as i8
    b[(off + 1) as usize] = ((v >> 8) & 0xFF) as i8
    b
}

fn emit_u32(buf: [i8; 4096], off: i64, v: i64) -> [i8; 4096] with Mut {
    var b = buf
    b[(off) as usize] = (v & 0xFF) as i8
    b[(off + 1) as usize] = ((v >> 8) & 0xFF) as i8
    b[(off + 2) as usize] = ((v >> 16) & 0xFF) as i8
    b[(off + 3) as usize] = ((v >> 24) & 0xFF) as i8
    b
}

fn emit_u64(buf: [i8; 4096], off: i64, v: i64) -> [i8; 4096] with Mut {
    var b = buf
    b[(off) as usize] = (v & 0xFF) as i8
    b[(off + 1) as usize] = ((v >> 8) & 0xFF) as i8
    b[(off + 2) as usize] = ((v >> 16) & 0xFF) as i8
    b[(off + 3) as usize] = ((v >> 24) & 0xFF) as i8
    b[(off + 4) as usize] = ((v >> 32) & 0xFF) as i8
    b[(off + 5) as usize] = ((v >> 40) & 0xFF) as i8
    b[(off + 6) as usize] = ((v >> 48) & 0xFF) as i8
    b[(off + 7) as usize] = ((v >> 56) & 0xFF) as i8
    b
}

fn main() -> i64 with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    // Build code: print_f64 at offset 0, then main stub
    var code = code_buffer_new()
    code = ast_emit_print_f64_builtin(code)
    let main_off = code.len
    code = emit_main(code, 0)  // print_f64 is at code offset 0

    let code_size = code.len
    let vaddr_base: i64 = 0x400000
    let code_file_off: i64 = 0x80  // After ELF header (64 bytes) + 1 program header (56 bytes) = 120 = 0x78, round up
    let entry_vaddr = vaddr_base + code_file_off + main_off

    // Build minimal ELF64 header
    var elf: [i8; 4096] = [0; 4096]

    // ELF magic: 7f 45 4c 46
    elf[0 as usize] = 0x7f as i8
    elf[1 as usize] = 0x45 as i8  // E
    elf[2 as usize] = 0x4c as i8  // L
    elf[3 as usize] = 0x46 as i8  // F

    // EI_CLASS=2 (64-bit), EI_DATA=1 (LE), EI_VERSION=1, EI_OSABI=0
    elf[4 as usize] = 2 as i8
    elf[5 as usize] = 1 as i8
    elf[6 as usize] = 1 as i8
    elf[7 as usize] = 0 as i8

    // e_type=2 (ET_EXEC), e_machine=0x3E (x86-64)
    elf = emit_u16(elf, 16, 2)
    elf = emit_u16(elf, 18, 0x3E)
    // e_version=1
    elf = emit_u32(elf, 20, 1)
    // e_entry
    elf = emit_u64(elf, 24, entry_vaddr)
    // e_phoff = 64 (right after ELF header)
    elf = emit_u64(elf, 32, 64)
    // e_shoff = 0 (no section headers)
    elf = emit_u64(elf, 40, 0)
    // e_flags = 0
    elf = emit_u32(elf, 48, 0)
    // e_ehsize = 64
    elf = emit_u16(elf, 52, 64)
    // e_phentsize = 56
    elf = emit_u16(elf, 54, 56)
    // e_phnum = 1
    elf = emit_u16(elf, 56, 1)
    // e_shentsize = 0
    elf = emit_u16(elf, 58, 0)
    // e_shnum = 0
    elf = emit_u16(elf, 60, 0)
    // e_shstrndx = 0
    elf = emit_u16(elf, 62, 0)

    // Program header (LOAD) at offset 64
    // p_type = 1 (PT_LOAD)
    elf = emit_u32(elf, 64, 1)
    // p_flags = 5 (PF_R | PF_X)
    elf = emit_u32(elf, 68, 5)
    // p_offset = 0
    elf = emit_u64(elf, 72, 0)
    // p_vaddr = vaddr_base
    elf = emit_u64(elf, 80, vaddr_base)
    // p_paddr = vaddr_base
    elf = emit_u64(elf, 88, vaddr_base)
    // p_filesz = code_file_off + code_size
    let total_file = code_file_off + code_size
    elf = emit_u64(elf, 96, total_file)
    // p_memsz = total_file
    elf = emit_u64(elf, 104, total_file)
    // p_align = 0x1000
    elf = emit_u64(elf, 112, 0x1000)

    // Copy code bytes into ELF at code_file_off
    var ci: i64 = 0
    while ci < code_size {
        elf[(code_file_off + ci) as usize] = code.bytes[ci as usize]
        ci = ci + 1
    }

    let elf_size = code_file_off + code_size

    // Write ELF to file using VM builtin
    let wr = write_file("/tmp/sprint235_f64.elf", elf, elf_size)
    if wr < 0 {
        print("FAIL: could not write ELF\n")
        return 1
    }

    print("PASS: ELF written size=")
    print_int(elf_size)
    print(" entry=0x")
    print_int(entry_vaddr)
    print(" code=")
    print_int(code_size)
    print("\n")
    0
}

comments: Tacrolimus oral SS trough propagation under Knightian uncertainty.
Mirrors tests/run-pass/vancomycin_propagation_v2.sio for the tacrolimus
clinical pathway. Three scenarios:
1. Pre-TDM (no samples) — wide Knightian band on F, Vc, CL. The 5 mg
q12h regimen for a 70 kg kidney-transplant maintenance patient
yields a C12h trough PBox of approximately [2.8, 17.6] ng/mL,
which straddles the 5–15 ng/mL therapeutic window → REFUSE.
2. Post-TDM (3 trough samples + CYP3A5 genotype) — narrow Knightian
band: PBox ≈ [5.2, 11.7] ng/mL ⊂ [5, 15] → PRESCRIBE.
3. Contract violation (weight 15 kg below [30, 200]) — vacuous PBox
with confidence 0 (CONTRACT_BLOCK).
This is the operational unit-test for stdlib/clinical/tacrolimus_oral_safety.sio
and the runtime witness for formal/lean4/SounioTacrolimusDosingSafety.lean.

instruction: Write a Sounio run-pass example named `tuple_return_sret_r12_slot`. A tuple-returning function that CALLS another tuple-returning function used to destroy its caller's aggregate-return pointer. The x86 SRET prologue is `push rbp; mov rbp,rsp; push r12; sub rsp,frame`, so. It should compile and run successfully. Expected stdout: TUPLE_SRET_R12_OK
description: A tuple-returning function that CALLS another tuple-returning function used to destroy its caller's aggregate-return pointer. The x86 SRET prologue is `push rbp; mov rbp,rsp; push r12; sub rsp,frame`, so
comments: A tuple-returning function that CALLS another tuple-returning function used to
destroy its caller's aggregate-return pointer.
The x86 SRET prologue is `push rbp; mov rbp,rsp; push r12; sub rsp,frame`, so
the saved r12 lives at rbp-0x08 -- which was also slot 1, where the incoming
SRET pointer was stored. `pop r12` then restored that pointer instead of the
caller's r12, and the caller wrote its result through a pointer into the
callee's dead frame. The next call reused those bytes, so every binding read
the LAST call's values.
Confirmed under gdb: r12 intact at the callee's entry, holding the callee's
own SRET at its `ret`. Fixed by reserving slot 1 for the pushed r12.
Two bindings minimum: with one, a stale pointer still reads its own values.

instruction: Write a Sounio run-pass example named `type_hash_3level_nesting`. Regression for the i64 type-hash overflow on 3-level pointer nesting (closed in 2523ee2f4 by composite-type interning in lean_single.sio). Pre-fix: ref_hash_make compounded the inner hash by *256 per level while. It should compile and run successfully. Expected stdout: type-hash 3-level PASS
description: Regression for the i64 type-hash overflow on 3-level pointer nesting (closed in 2523ee2f4 by composite-type interning in lean_single.sio). Pre-fix: ref_hash_make compounded the inner hash by *256 per level while
comments: Regression for the i64 type-hash overflow on 3-level pointer nesting
(closed in 2523ee2f4 by composite-type interning in lean_single.sio).
Pre-fix: ref_hash_make compounded the inner hash by *256 per level while
the inner still carried the 2^50 band, so &Option<Box<Struct>> wrapped
mod 2^64 and corrupted the struct hash — field access reported
"unknown field" and shapes collided.
Post-fix: composite inners are interned (CT_INNER_HASH[4096]) and only
a small surrogate id is multiplied, keeping the encoded hash inside
[2^50, 2^51) at arbitrary depth.
This fixture exercises field access through two structurally distinct
3-level nestings simultaneously to assert they do not alias: the same
compile unit creates and reads both &Option<Box<A>> and &Option<Box<B>>.
Under the bug, the two struct hashes would collide after the ×256 wrap
(different inner structs, same wrapped surrogate), so the field offsets
would be wrong for at least one of them.

instruction: Write a Sounio run-pass example named `u64_const_fold_witness`. Finding 11 (issue #2084): const_prop folds u64 >>, /, % with unsigned semantics — without this, fold_binop_int would treat operands as i64 and produce the wrong magnitudes at bit 63. It should compile and run successfully.
description: Finding 11 (issue #2084): const_prop folds u64 >>, /, % with unsigned semantics — without this, fold_binop_int would treat operands as i64 and produce the wrong magnitudes at bit 63.
comments: Finding 11 (issue #2084): const_prop folds u64 >>, /, % with unsigned
semantics — without this, fold_binop_int would treat operands as i64
and produce the wrong magnitudes at bit 63.
Witnesses 4 cases that all hit the literal-only fold path (no binary
IR ever gets emitted for these expressions; they compile to IrLoadImm
via const_prop ->  cp_u64_div / cp_u64_mod / cp_u64_shr):
0xFFFF_FFFF_FFFF_FFFF_u64 /  2   == 0x7FFF_FFFF_FFFF_FFFF   (cp_u64_div)
0xFFFF_FFFF_FFFF_FFFF_u64 >> 4   == 0x0FFF_FFFF_FFFF_FFFF  (cp_u64_shr)
0xFFFF_FFFF_FFFF_FFFF_u64 >> 64  == 0                      (cp_u64_shr, n>=64)
The equality comparisons then anchor the folded values at runtime.
Under the signed fold path these would each be a different number:
0xFFFF.. / 2  = 0          in i64 truncate-toward-zero
0xFFFF.. % 3  = -1         in i64 truncate-toward-zero
0xFFFF.. >> 4 = 0xFFFFFFFF in i64 arithmetic shift
0xFFFF.. >> 64 = (out of range, BOTTOM -> no fold)
and each assert below would catch that signed result.

description: Minimal reproducer for ζ — GUM variance deep-chain bug. See docs/research/zeta_variance_fix_plan.md and feedback_variance_deep_chains.md for the full analysis.
comments: Minimal reproducer for ζ — GUM variance deep-chain bug.
See docs/research/zeta_variance_fix_plan.md and
feedback_variance_deep_chains.md for the full analysis.
Symptom: enough distinct `let` bindings in a single function body push
the compiler's NEXT_SLOT counter past the 1024-slot variance shadow
buffer cap. Subsequent variance_of() reads return 0 or 2^63-scale garbage.
Trigger confirmed in tests/run-pass/rapamycin_epistemic_adaptive.sio —
that test prints ch1=ch2=9.22e18 (exactly 2^63) after ~70 adaptive steps.
This reproducer isolates the pattern: >300 distinct let bindings in a
single function, with variance propagated through a chain of function
calls that each emit multiple variance_addsub / variance_muldiv ops.
Current status (2026-04-12): this test PASSES on the current compiler
because the slot threshold isn't hit with the minimal pattern below —
the bug requires the specific structure of rapamycin_epistemic_adaptive.
Kept as a skeleton / smoke test. A true overflow-triggering minimal
reproducer is an open sub-task of ζ.

instruction: Write a Sounio run-pass example named `zd_unlearning_full_basis`. machine-unlearning with a 4-generator contribution — the old 2-of-4 projection leaves g1/g2 residual, the fixed stdlib forget_contribution (4-of-4) erases it exactly. It should compile and run successfully.
description: machine-unlearning with a 4-generator contribution — the old 2-of-4 projection leaves g1/g2 residual, the fixed stdlib forget_contribution (4-of-4) erases it exactly
comments: Full Test Suite CI uses souc-stage2 (lean_single). Madaros runs this graph.
examples/zd_machine_unlearning.sio uses an INLINE 2-vector projection (g0,g3)
and places Alice only on those two generators, so it never exercises the full
kernel. This test constructs a contribution that spans all four generators and
shows the difference the #2111 fix makes:
OLD (2-of-4, replicated inline): Alice's g1/g2 components SURVIVE forgetting.
NEW (stdlib forget_contribution): the whole contribution is erased, exact.
Integer coefficients ⇒ exact comparisons.

description: machine-unlearning with a 4-generator contribution — the old 2-of-4 projection leaves g1/g2 residual, the fixed stdlib forget_contribution (4-of-4) erases it exactly

instruction: Write a Sounio compile-fail example named `cond_indep_violation`. conditional independence violation — a variable declared independent of itself. It should fail to compile. The compiler output should include: E072.
description: conditional independence violation — a variable declared independent of itself
comments: This test used to be disabled, with the claim it checks written only as a
comment, because no surface syntax could produce IndepKnowledge. The type kind
existed in the checker and nothing could reach it. Now the grammar exists and
the test asserts against the compiler instead of describing what it would say.
Do not write the skip annotation in prose here: the harness matches that string
anywhere in the file, so mentioning it silently turns this test off.
A variable is never independent of itself: P(X, X) = P(X)·P(X) only in the
degenerate case. So `IndepKnowledge<f64, x, x>` asserts nothing — and asserting
nothing is exactly how an unfounded quadrature gets licensed, since the
composition law in stdlib/epistemic/graded_effects.sio grants the tighter
bound to any claim that type-checks.
The full Pearl d-separation check (Bayes Ball, causal.sio) is NOT what rejects
this. No causal graph can be declared in source yet, so nothing can discharge
a well-formed claim. What the compiler enforces here is the one rule it can
know without a graph — and it enforces it rather than assuming it.
Reference: Pearl 1995, d-separation; Bayes Ball (Shachter 1998).

description: conditional independence violation — a variable declared independent of itself

instruction: Write a Sounio compile-fail example named `correlate_rho_must_be_literal`. The correlation coefficient must fold at compile time. lower_correlate_call_ref keeps rho as an f64, not a register, and reads it only from a literal. A runtime third argument therefore never propagates --. It should fail to compile. The compiler output should include: E243.
description: The correlation coefficient must fold at compile time. lower_correlate_call_ref keeps rho as an f64, not a register, and reads it only from a literal. A runtime third argument therefore never propagates --
comments: The correlation coefficient must fold at compile time.
lower_correlate_call_ref keeps rho as an f64, not a register, and reads it
only from a literal. A runtime third argument therefore never propagates --
it leaves rho at its initialiser, 0.0, which is not "no correlation given"
but the positive assertion that the two channels are independent. The one
claim `correlate` exists to make deniable was being fabricated in silence,
on the path where the programmer had explicitly said otherwise.
There is no lowering to fall back on, so refusal is the only honest answer.

comments: The case that separates real d-separation from a reachability check.
dor and sono are marginally independent: the only path between them meets
head-to-head at registro, and a collider blocks by default. Conditioning on
registro OPENS that path (Berkson 1946) — so adding `| registro` turns a true
claim into a false one. Conditioning is not monotonically helpful, and a
checker that assumed it were would accept exactly this.

instruction: Write a Sounio compile-fail example named `effect_mut_generated_at_excl_ref_store`. Regression pin for #1488 — the effect system had no leaf-level source of Mut. Madaros propagated declared effects correctly: a caller of a `with Mut` callee was required to declare it too. What was missing was anything that INTRODUCED. It should fail to compile. description: Regression pin for #1488 — the effect system had no leaf-level source of Mut. Madaros propagated declared effects correctly: a caller of a `with Mut` callee was required to declare it too. What was missing was anything that INTRODUCED
comments: Regression pin for #1488 — the effect system had no leaf-level source of Mut.
Madaros propagated declared effects correctly: a caller of a `with Mut` callee
was required to declare it too. What was missing was anything that INTRODUCED
the effect at the point where mutation actually happens. So this function
type-checked with no `with Mut`, and because nothing below it ever asserted the
effect, no caller above it could be required to carry it either. `with Mut` was
true only where a human had written it — the guarantee was vacuous exactly at
the leaves, which is where it has to hold.
Measured before the fix: Madaros accepted this (exit 0). lean_single rejected
it. A dead-code explanation was ruled out separately: Madaros already rejected
a caller of a callee that DECLARES `with Mut`, even when that caller is
unreachable from main, so propagation was working and only generation was
absent.
`requires: madaros` because the fix lives in the modular checker; lean_single
has always rejected this shape and the stage2 suite would pass it for a
different reason.

description: hessian_of(expr, j, k) over 8 channels; sensitivity_of(x, k) over 32. Before E242 these compiled and answered 0.000000. In this algebra a zero is not a neutral value: zero variance means "certain", zero sensitivity means
comments: hessian_of(expr, j, k) over 8 channels; sensitivity_of(x, k) over 32.
Before E242 these compiled and answered 0.000000. In this algebra a zero is
not a neutral value: zero variance means "certain", zero sensitivity means
"does not depend on", zero Hessian means "no second-order dependence". They
are the strongest claims the system can make, and they were being handed
back silently in exactly the cases where it knew least -- an index it has no
channel for.
`0 - 1` is how this dialect spells a negative literal, so the index check
has to fold it. Reading only ExprIntLit let hessian_of(x*x, 0 - 1, 0)
through, and the refusal gate caught that on the run meant to prove it green.

comments: Gradient Topology Types (GTT) — scrutinee→bound-var VAR_CH_SET seeding.
Without scrutinee→bound-var VAR_CH_SET seeding, the bound variable
inside a match arm carries a stale 0 in `VAR_CH_SET[vb_slot]`.  When
arm-body code loads the bound variable, its EXPR_CH_SET becomes 0
("unknown topology" in GTT terminology), which makes the
`hessian_of` check at `compile_primary:~8598` SILENTLY SKIP the
GTT refusal — the `b7h_ch_set != 0` guard deliberately falls through
when topology is unknown.  Result: out-of-topology `hessian_of` on a
bound variable accepts incorrectly.
With the fix, the bound variable inherits the scrutinee's declared
topology (`VAR_CH_SET[vb_slot] = match_scrut_ch_set`).  Since the
scrutinee here carries topology `{ch 0}`, and we ask for
`hessian_of(v, 2, 2)` (channel 2 not in {ch 0}), the check fires
and this program is correctly REFUSED at typecheck.
This is the direct downstream guarantee of week-7 stage 1's Lean
theorem `Typing.tMatch`: `v.footprint ⊆ Sc ∪ (Ss i)` per `gtt_sound`
— a bound variable alias of the scrutinee inherits the scrutinee's
channel set.

comments: Gradient Topology Types (GTT) — β⁹ week-10 compile-fail (reassignment replaces topology).
After the scalar-reassignment fix, `x = new_expr` REPLACES VAR_CH_SET[x]
with EXPR_CH_SET of the new expression (not unioned).  So:
var r = k0.value     // r: {ch0}

reflects its *current* value's topology, not its history.

comments: indep_dsep_forged_literal_madaros
Regression for a live defect (merged, then fast-followed): `indep_dsep`
used to take `proof: i64` and compare it to the literal 1, so a hand-typed
`indep_dsep(1)` was accepted identically to a discharged
`indep_dsep(d_separated(A, B | Z))` witness -- there was no such thing as a
forged proof, because both reached the function as the same value with the
same type. See indep_dsep_forged_literal_lean_single.sio for the other
engine's variant of this same test.
On Madaros the fix is a real opaque type: `proof: DsepProof`, where
`DsepProof` names no `struct { ... }` anywhere in the tree, so no source
text can construct one via a literal, and `types_compatible` (compat.sio)
makes it compatible with nothing but itself. `indep_dsep(1)` therefore
fails the ordinary, structurally-guaranteed argument-type check -- E009,
not a dedicated diagnostic, because there is nothing dedicated to fail:
an i64 can never satisfy this parameter, for any value.
`requires: madaros` because the diagnostic is a genuine engine difference:
lean_single has no comparable opaque-type mechanism and rejects this same
program a different way (E257, a syntactic check over the witness the
compiler itself produced) -- see the lean_single-only sibling file.

description: requires: madaros because IR_MAX_INSTRS is a Madaros IR limit. lean_single -- which the CI full-test-suite runs -- has no such wall and compiles this file happily, so without the guard this is a false red. That is exactly how it
comments: requires: madaros because IR_MAX_INSTRS is a Madaros IR limit. lean_single --
which the CI full-test-suite runs -- has no such wall and compiles this file
happily, so without the guard this is a false red. That is exactly how it
failed the first time it was pushed.
#1645: a function past IR_MAX_INSTRS had its remaining instructions DROPPED and
the compile still exited 0, writing a binary whose tail was simply missing. The
program ran, printed nothing after the cut, and exited 0 as well -- the "empty
green" shape reported in #1586 on a ~1190-line main.
Why it survived: Lowerer is threaded by VALUE. `emit` writes the instruction
through a Box, so the truncation is permanent and visible in the finished
module, but `had_error` is a plain scalar field of the Lowerer value -- any link
in the lowering chain that discards the Lowerer it was handed loses the flag
while keeping the damage. Measured: instr_count pinned at exactly 4096 and
had_error FALSE, so all six `if body_result.had_error` checks passed.
The fix records the wall somewhere value semantics cannot reach and ORs it into
every IrLowerResult at construction, so the existing consumers work unchanged.
This file must stay ONE function: the wall is per function, so splitting it
across helpers is exactly the workaround that hid the defect.
~330 statements of this shape lower to more than 4096 IR instructions.

(self-hosted/ir/lower.sio) has no Knowledge arm. Both operands lower as

RIGHT operand's value, silently, at exit 0 -- while `+`, `-` and `/` compiled
clean and segfaulted at runtime. A silent wrong answer that sometimes crashes
is strictly worse than a diagnostic, so the checker now refuses it.
The mixed forms (`kA * 2.0`, `2.0 * kA`, `kA + 2.0`) were already refused.
lean_single implements all of this correctly; see #1706 for the engine table.

IDENTIFIERS now has a real, measured-correct lowering (value'=v1+v2,
variance'=var1+var2 -- ordinary independent addition, no covariance term,
none of the sign/norm ambiguity Sub/Mul/Div still carry) -- see
tests/run-pass/correlated_independent_measures_ok.sio and
checker_is_knowledge_ident_add's E245 exemption in check.sio, which fires

keeps proving `+` still refuses in general -- only the narrower bare-ident

description: requires: madaros is truthful here and load-bearing. CI's Full Test Suite runs souc-stage2, which selfhost_host_gate.sh builds from self-hosted/compiler/ lean_single.sio -- a self-contained file with its own checker. lean_single
comments: requires: madaros is truthful here and load-bearing. CI's Full Test Suite runs
souc-stage2, which selfhost_host_gate.sh builds from self-hosted/compiler/
lean_single.sio -- a self-contained file with its own checker. lean_single
IMPLEMENTS Knowledge arithmetic correctly, so it does not refuse this and must
not be asked to. E245 lives in the modular checker, which only Madaros runs.
Arithmetic between two Knowledge<T> values typechecks but has no lowering.
checker_check_binary_with_operand_types_inplace routes through
knowledge_binary_result and returns Knowledge<T>, but lower_binary_expr_ref
(self-hosted/ir/lower.sio) has no Knowledge arm. Both operands lower as
scalars, and a Knowledge operand lowers to the object handle -- so `kA * kB`
multiplies two pointers and `.value` on the result dereferences an arbitrary
address.
Measured on Madaros before this refusal: `*` returned 3.0 for 2.0*3.0 -- the
RIGHT operand's value, silently, at exit 0 -- while `+`, `-` and `/` compiled
clean and segfaulted at runtime. A silent wrong answer that sometimes crashes
is strictly worse than a diagnostic, so the checker now refuses it.
The mixed forms (`kA * 2.0`, `2.0 * kA`, `kA + 2.0`) were already refused.
lean_single implements all of this correctly; see #1706 for the engine table.

comments: N3 (E230) anti-garbling, the canonical case. `x + x` adds a measured value
to itself: both operands carry the SAME noise symbol, so the true variance of
the sum is 4*Var(x), but the independence-assuming `+` computes
Var(x) + Var(x) = 2*Var(x) -- half the truth, precision the input does not
justify. The rule refuses it.
The epistemic dual of R-ORIGIN (E222): where that refuses manufacturing where
a value CAME FROM, this refuses manufacturing HOW PRECISE it is.
Sabotage (SOUNIO_NS_DISABLE=1) turns off ONLY the anti-garbling refusal; under
it this file compiles, proving the refusal is the noise-symbol rule and not an
unrelated error further up.

N3 (E230) anti-garbling, the conservative case. `mystery()` returns a Knowledge whose source-set the checker cannot project through the call, so it is UNKNOWN (top). Adding it to a measured value might or might not share a. It should fail to compile. The compiler output should include: independence-assuming operation over correlated uncertainty.
description: N3 (E230) anti-garbling, the conservative case. `mystery()` returns a Knowledge whose source-set the checker cannot project through the call, so it is UNKNOWN (top). Adding it to a measured value might or might not share a
comments: N3 (E230) anti-garbling, the conservative case. `mystery()` returns a
Knowledge whose source-set the checker cannot project through the call, so it
is UNKNOWN (top). Adding it to a measured value might or might not share a
source; the rule cannot PROVE the sources disjoint, so it fails closed and
refuses. Unknown is never treated as disjoint -- assuming independence one
cannot certify is exactly the anti-garbling this rule exists to prevent.
(This is the same program as the N2 witness ns_unknown_absorb_trace, which
observed union(top, {s}) = top under SOUNIO_NS_TRACE. Under N3 that operation
is refused, so this compile-fail fixture supersedes it as the top-operand
witness -- see the N3 handoff note.)
Sabotage (SOUNIO_NS_DISABLE=1) makes the refusal vanish, proving it is the NS
rule and not an unrelated error.

instruction: Write a Sounio compile-fail example named `ns_add_via_identity_rejected`. N3 (E230) anti-garbling, the laundering-through-identity case (Paper A control 4: `ident(x) + x`). `ident` is an exact parameter projection, so the N2 call-projection rule carries x's noise-symbol set THROUGH the call: the. It should fail to compile. The compiler output should include: independence-assuming operation over correlated uncertainty.
description: N3 (E230) anti-garbling, the laundering-through-identity case (Paper A control 4: `ident(x) + x`). `ident` is an exact parameter projection, so the N2 call-projection rule carries x's noise-symbol set THROUGH the call: the
comments: N3 (E230) anti-garbling, the laundering-through-identity case (Paper A
control 4: `ident(x) + x`). `ident` is an exact parameter projection, so the
N2 call-projection rule carries x's noise-symbol set THROUGH the call: the
two operands of `+` still share x's source and the independence-assuming
add is refused. Without projection the call would default to top, which is
ALSO refused (top is never disjoint) -- so this fixture cannot pass by
either route; what it pins is that a projection does not launder a source.
The `+ Knowledge(0.0, ε = 0.05)` step and the explicit `epsilon < 1.0`
clause on ident's parameter are the same E036 call-boundary workaround used
by tests/run-pass/ns_ident_preserves_distinct_trace.sio (pre-existing gap,
not part of the NS wire): union with an empty-set literal keeps the measured
singleton handle while giving the value a boundary-passing epsilon.
Sabotage (SOUNIO_NS_DISABLE=1) makes E230 vanish, proving the refusal is the
noise-symbol rule and not an unrelated error. (On Madaros the same line is
also refused by E245 -- Knowledge x Knowledge arithmetic has no lowering,
#1706 -- which stays under the knob; the two are independent.)

instruction: Write a Sounio compile-fail example named `ns_rem_result_is_opaque`. REGRESSION WITNESS for a fail-open W4 introduced and math-review caught (grok-4.6, 2026-09-02). The signed domain gave Sub an escape hatch: a non-disjoint pair is ALLOWED. It should fail to compile. The compiler output should include: independence-assuming operation over correlated uncertainty.
description: REGRESSION WITNESS for a fail-open W4 introduced and math-review caught (grok-4.6, 2026-09-02). The signed domain gave Sub an escape hatch: a non-disjoint pair is ALLOWED
comments: REGRESSION WITNESS for a fail-open W4 introduced and math-review caught
The signed domain gave Sub an escape hatch: a non-disjoint pair is ALLOWED
when ns_cov_nonneg proves every shared source carries a non-negative
coefficient product. That certificate is only as good as the signs feeding
it, and the transfer originally sent every operator except Sub, Mul and Div
through ns_union -- the ADDITIVE join. OpRem landed there. So
r = a % b        published a's and b's additive signs as if they were r's
s = r - a        found `a` at + in both operands, certified Cov >= 0,
and COMPILED
but Rem's Jacobian signs are not the additive join of its operands' signs, so
that certificate was unfounded and Var(r - a) could be understated -- the
exact thing E230 exists to refuse, reintroduced through the new escape hatch
rather than through the rule it guards.
The fix makes ns_union_opaque the DEFAULT and ns_union the exception (OpAdd
only): an operator nobody has modelled marks its result sign-unknown, and
ns_cov_nonneg fails closed on it. This file must stay refused. If it ever
compiles again, the transfer has gone back to trusting signs it cannot derive.

instruction: Write a Sounio compile-fail example named `ns_source_cap_overflow_loud`. W4 LOUD-OVERFLOW witness (E178). Before W4 the source cap degraded SILENTLY: the 65th measure() saturated its handle to unknown (-1), ns_disjoint then refused to certify anything against it, and every downstream combination was. It should fail to compile. The compiler output should include: noise-source capacity exceeded.
description: W4 LOUD-OVERFLOW witness (E178). Before W4 the source cap degraded SILENTLY: the 65th measure() saturated its handle to unknown (-1), ns_disjoint then refused to certify anything against it, and every downstream combination was
comments: W4 LOUD-OVERFLOW witness (E178). Before W4 the source cap degraded SILENTLY:
the 65th measure() saturated its handle to unknown (-1), ns_disjoint then
refused to certify anything against it, and every downstream combination was
refused by E230 with no indication that the analysis had simply run out of
room. An overflow that only shows up as a wall of unrelated-looking refusals
-- or, in an engine that propagates rather than refuses, as an uncertainty
band that is quietly wrong -- is the exact failure mode this witness exists to
prevent.
The cap is now 256 (ns_source_cap(), four 64-bit words). Sources 0..255 are
representable; m256 and m257 are not, and each one reports E178 AT ITS OWN
measure() SITE. The handle still saturates to unknown, so the analysis stays
sound -- it is now merely also honest.
There is deliberately no arithmetic in this body: the file must fail for the
capacity reason and nothing else.

instruction: Write a Sounio compile-fail example named `ns_sub_opposite_sign_rejected`. W4, the case the N3 scope note named explicitly: an OPPOSITE-SIGN shared source under subtraction is a genuine anti-garbling, and it used to pass unrefused. It should fail to compile. The compiler output should include: independence-assuming operation over correlated uncertainty.
description: W4, the case the N3 scope note named explicitly: an OPPOSITE-SIGN shared source under subtraction is a genuine anti-garbling, and it used to pass unrefused.
comments: W4, the case the N3 scope note named explicitly: an OPPOSITE-SIGN shared
source under subtraction is a genuine anti-garbling, and it used to pass
unrefused.
d = p - a          d carries a with coefficient -1
s = d - a          a appears as (-1) on the left and (+1) on the right
True variance: Var(s) = Var(p - 2a) = Var p + 4 Var a.
Independence-assuming: Var d + Var a = (Var p + Var a) + Var a
= Var p + 2 Var a.
The reported band is SMALLER than the truth -- precision the inputs do not
justify -- because the dropped term is -2 Cov(d, a) with Cov(d, a) < 0.
ns_union_sub records the negation, so ns_cov_nonneg finds a bit in
(neg_d & pos_a) and refuses to certify Cov >= 0. Contrast
ns_sub_same_sign_allowed_trace.sio, where the same-sign reuse `x - x` is
still accepted because there the naive variance OVERSTATES.

description: W4 (E230 extended to Sub): a shared source whose COEFFICIENT SIGN cannot be established. `a * b` produces a value whose first-order form lives in the relative basis -- its coefficients are not comparable with the additive ones
comments: W4 (E230 extended to Sub): a shared source whose COEFFICIENT SIGN cannot be
established. `a * b` produces a value whose first-order form lives in the
relative basis -- its coefficients are not comparable with the additive ones

UNDERSTATE if Cov < 0. Fail closed: refuse.
This is the scope hole the N3 comment recorded as future work ("a full
sign-of-covariance treatment of Sub/Div"). It is now closed.

comments: β⁸ Phase 2 compile-fail: non-associative algebra multiplication with an active
AD shadow slot must be refused when the algebra lacks `reassociate: fano_selective`.
Gate location: self-hosted/compiler/lean_single.sio (op==19 binary section)
Formal proof:  formal/NonAssocHessian.lean — `refusal_is_sound`
Trigger mechanism:
`compile_primary()` resets EXPR_SSHADOW = -1 at entry, then each field
compile also resets it.  With a SINGLE-basis algebra, `OctScalar { e0: km.value }`
compiles only one field — km.value sets EXPR_SSHADOW = 0 and no subsequent
field resets it.  The struct literal returns with EXPR_TY=6, EXPR_SSHADOW=0.
That state is captured into left_sshadow = 0 before compiling the right operand.
The gate then sees:
- left_ty == 6 (algebra struct), al_is_algebra → true
- al_mul_is_associative(OctScalar_hash) == false  (alternative mul)
- has_shadow == true  (left_sshadow = 0 >= 0)
- al_reassoc_mode == 0  (no fano_selective declared)
⇒ tc_linear_violation fires → typecheck: failed → exit 1.

instruction: Write a Sounio compile-fail example named `potential_outcome_both_observed`. potential outcome linear violation — cannot observe both Y(0) and Y(1) for same unit. It should fail to compile. The compiler output should include: E073. This example is currently marked ignored in the upstream test suite.
description: potential outcome linear violation — cannot observe both Y(0) and Y(1) for same unit
comments: The Fundamental Problem of Causal Inference (Holland 1986):
For any unit i, only ONE of {Y_i(0), Y_i(1)} can ever be observed.
Y_i(0) = outcome under control; Y_i(1) = outcome under treatment.
Sounio enforces this via linear types: PotentialOutcome<T> is consumed on observation.
Attempting to use BOTH Y(0) and Y(1) for the same unit violates the linear type constraint (E073).
This tests the PO track (Sprint 20): TyPotentialOutcome<T> as a linearly-consumed type.
The individual treatment effect ITE = Y(1) - Y(0) is unobservable for any single unit;
only the Average Treatment Effect ATE = E[Y(1) - Y(0)] can be estimated from a population.
Reference: Holland 1986, Rubin 1974, Imbens & Rubin 2015 (Causal Inference for Statistics).

description: potential outcome linear violation — cannot observe both Y(0) and Y(1) for same unit

description: quadrature cannot be obtained without a discharged proof of independence
comments: The whole chain, at its narrowest point.
graded_compose_indep grants the tight uncertainty bound — JCGM 100:2008
eq. (10) — only to a witness of kind d-separated. That witness can only be
built by indep_dsep, and indep_dsep only accepts the result of the
compiler-checked `d_separated(A, B | Z)` form.
Here hora is a common cause of both hrv and kp, so hrv and kp are NOT
marginally independent. The proof is requested without conditioning on hora,
the graph refuses it, and the tight bound is unreachable. Writing
`| hora` is what makes this compile — which is exactly the point: the
conditioning set is not decoration, it is the content of the claim.
