comments: A refinement must hold at the RETURN, not only at a binding.
This is the Madaros half of a measured engine divergence. On main@88c2ab8ee8
the *mut checker spine calls checker_check_refinement_literal_inplace from
exactly two places (check.sio:9627, 9687), both in the let/var handlers, and
check/compat.sio never looks at refinement_id. So under Madaros a refinement
is enforced where a value is BOUND and nowhere else:
$ artifacts/madaros --check tests/compile-fail/refinement_f64_return_violation.sio
check: OK
lean_single rejects the same file. tests/known_failures/
hardened_diagnostics_full_suite.txt records the split in its own words
(2026-08-23): "default Madaros still answers `check: OK` on that file, so the
refinement is unenforced there; that is a compiler defect, not a manifest
one." This test is that defect, pinned for the integer case.
SCOPE. checker_check_refinement_literal_inplace only fires when
last_literal_kind is 1 (int) or 2 (float), so this pins the LITERAL return.
The propagated case is a separate, still-open hole:
fn lift(x: i64) -> { n: i64 | n >= 0 } { x }        // still accepted
fn f() -> { n: i64 | n >= 0 } { let b = 0 - 7  return b }  // still accepted
Those need dataflow the checker does not have here; main's own
tests/compile-fail/refinement_return_var.sio pins that case for lean_single
and is untouched by this test. Closing the literal case is what the
known-failures manifest asks for, and is where the fix stops.
The refinement is written INLINE, not through a `type` alias. A named alias
takes a different path on the *mut spine (checker_lower_named_type_mut does
not consult the refinement table) and fails with E008 "expected Fp, found
i64" long before the refinement is consulted -- a separate, unfixed defect
that this test deliberately does not depend on.

instruction: Write a Sounio compile-fail example named `refinement_subtype_strict`. refinement_subtype_strict The pattern used to read E001, which this program never emits — it is rejected by the refinement checker with an uncoded diagnostic. The harness was not. It should fail to compile. The compiler output should include: refinement type violation.
description: refinement_subtype_strict The pattern used to read E001, which this program never emits — it is rejected by the refinement checker with an uncoded diagnostic. The harness was not
comments: refinement_subtype_strict
The pattern used to read E001, which this program never emits — it is rejected
by the refinement checker with an uncoded diagnostic. The harness was not
matching error-pattern at all, so the test passed while asserting the wrong
thing; with the matcher fixed the annotation had to say what is actually
emitted.
`requires: lean_single` because the diagnostic this asserts is an engine
difference, not a language rule. Measured 2026-09-03 on both:
lean_single  error[E208]: refinement type violation — value 0 does not
satisfy parameter predicate at line 19        ← what is asserted
Madaros      error[E008] return value does not match declared return type
error[E001] this binding expects a different type
error[E009] argument type does not match parameter
Madaros is not missing the diagnostic — check.sio carries code 42, "value does
not satisfy the refinement predicate". It never reaches it, because it relates
a refinement type to its base type in NEITHER direction:
fn f(x: Positive) -> i32 { x }    E008, though every Positive IS an i32
let p: Positive = 0               E001, a bare type mismatch standing where
the predicate should have spoken
So the three errors above are all one gap wearing three codes, and the E009 at
the call site rejects for the wrong reason: NonNeg and Positive differ as
NAMES, not because 0 fails `n > 0`. Two identical refinement names with a
violated predicate would slip through it.
Erasure (Positive → i32) would be sound to open on its own. The introduction
direction is where the predicate must actually be evaluated, and opening it
without first proving the check fires would turn a wrongly-coded rejection
into an acceptance — a fail-open in a type system. Left for whoever implements
refinement subsumption in the modular checker, rather than half-done here.

instruction: Write a Sounio compile-fail example named `tac_compile_gate_refuse`. Dissertation contribution #2 (compile-time confidence gate) — REFUSE path. `prescribe_tac` is annotated `with Confidence(800)`. The body must carry compile-time confidence ≥ 800/1000 on every expression token. It should fail to compile. The compiler output should include: EpistemicComplete violation.
description: Dissertation contribution #2 (compile-time confidence gate) — REFUSE path. `prescribe_tac` is annotated `with Confidence(800)`. The body must carry compile-time confidence ≥ 800/1000 on every expression token.
comments: Dissertation contribution #2 (compile-time confidence gate) — REFUSE path.
`prescribe_tac` is annotated `with Confidence(800)`. The body must carry
compile-time confidence ≥ 800/1000 on every expression token.
`measure(8.0, uncertainty: 4.0)` yields confidence = 1 − 4.0/8.0 = 0.5
= 500/1000, BELOW the 800 threshold. The compiler is required to
REJECT this program — no binary is emitted, the rejection is enforced
before any runtime check would run. Diagnostic from
lean_single.sio:20984-21006 prints
`error: EpistemicComplete violation in fn main ... (conf=500 < 800)`.
Clinical narrative: pre-TDM (n=0 samples), the only available C24h
estimate is the wide popPK prior with CV ≥ 50%. The compile-time
rejection prevents code that would prescribe under insufficient
evidence — a guarantee runtime gates cannot give.

description: #1634: one stray closing brace used to compile to a scatter of `E200` lines in a DIFFERENT file, naming a parameter that had nothing to do with it, and `typecheck: failed` with no `error:` line at all -- so `grep '^error'` on the
comments: #1634: one stray closing brace used to compile to a scatter of `E200` lines
in a DIFFERENT file, naming a parameter that had nothing to do with it, and
`typecheck: failed` with no `error:` line at all -- so `grep '^error'` on the
build log returned nothing and the build read as having failed for no stated
reason. It cost a day of bisection on PR #1630.
The mechanism: lean_single's Pass 0b tracked brace depth with an UNCLAMPED
decrement, so one extra `}` pinned depth negative for the rest of the token
stream. Past that point every function-body `var` registered as a global, and
the function body spans that pass 1b derives shifted, so parameters
registered for function i were checked against function j's body.
The diagnostic must name the file and the line, and must carry an `error:`
prefix. Nine `E200`s pointing at innocent code is not a diagnostic.

comments: This was tests/known-gaps/units/derived_unit_dropped_by_inference.sio, a

quotient lost its dimension, so mol/cm3 + K compiled. It is here, and not

file along with the rest of the corpus.
